items.title: Ghana wins bid to chair UN Tourism Executive Council for 2027
items.description: Ghana has secured the Chairmanship of the UN Tourism Executive Council for 2027 after polling 19 votes to defeat Argentina, which garnered 14 votes, at the 127th Executive Council meeting in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. The victory places Ghana in a strategic leadership position within global tourism governance and reinforces the country’s growing influence in shaping international tourism policy and cooperation. Ghana’s bid was spearheaded by the Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, who formally expressed the country’s interest in the position in a letter to the Secretary-General of UN Tourism in Madrid, Spain, dated November 24, 2026. The Minister underscored Ghana’s commitment to the objectives of UN Tourism and its willingness to contribute meaningfully to the Organisation’s work and the advancement of global tourism. “As an active and committed member of the Organisation, Ghana remains dedicated to advancing the objectives of UN Tourism and contributing meaningfully to the development of global tourism,” she stated. She further noted that Ghana’s aspiration to lead the Council was driven by the desire to strengthen collaboration among Member States, enhance the Council’s effectiveness and support the implementation of the Organisation’s mandate. The Minister for Tourism also emphasised Ghana’s interest in providing a platform for articulating and advancing Africa’s collective interests and perspectives while contributing to the broader priorities of UN Tourism. The Executive Council is UN Tourism’s key governing body responsible for ensuring the effective implementation of the Organisation’s work programme, overseeing its budget and policy direction, and providing strategic guidance on matters relating to international tourism development. Ghana’s one-year Chairmanship, which will run through 2027, is expected to provide an opportunity for the country to advance key tourism priorities, including sustainable tourism development, investment promotion, cultural and heritage tourism, youth empowerment, climate resilience and inclusive growth for local communities. The achievement also comes at a significant time for Ghana, as the country prepares to host the 70th Session of the UN Tourism Commission for Africa (CAF) in 2027, coinciding with its 70th Independence Anniversary. Ghana is expected to leverage the Chairmanship to deepen cooperation among Member States, strengthen Africa’s voice in international tourism discourse and promote tourism as a catalyst for employment, investment, cultural exchange and sustainable economic development.

items.title: FIFM : Othmane Zine, le regard marocain derrière « Leïla et la nuit »
items.description: Présenté en première mondiale dans la section Gala du Festival international du film de Marrakech, « Leïla et la nuit » est le fruit d’une co-réalisation entre le Brésilien Fellipe Barbosa et le Marocain Othmane Zine. Mais derrière cette collaboration franco-maroco-brésilienne se cache surtout une histoire d’amitié ancienne et un lien intime avec la famille Alaoui. Co-scénariste et co-réalisateur du film, Othmane Zine apporte un regard marocain essentiel à une œuvre qui ne cherche pas à raconter la vie de Leïla Alaoui, mais à sonder ce que sa disparition a laissé derrière elle. Pour Othmane Zine, « Leïla et la nuit » ne pouvait être un projet comme les autres. Le réalisateur marocain connaissait Leïla Alaoui depuis l’enfance. « Leïla et moi, on se connaît depuis qu’on a l’âge de 5 ans », raconte-t-il. Une proximité qui s’est étendue à toute la famille et qui explique, en partie, la naissance naturelle de cette co-réalisation. Lorsque Leïla part étudier aux États-Unis au début des années 2000, elle y rencontre Fellipe Barbosa. Leur amitié devient rapidement très forte et le jeune cinéaste brésilien découvre à son tour le Maroc, où il passe un été auprès de Leïla et de ses amis. Les liens se poursuivent au fil des années. Zine collaborera notamment avec Barbosa sur son premier long métrage, « Casa Grande ». Lorsque Leïla est tuée en 2016 dans l’attaque de Ouagadougou, puis que son père Aziz Alaoui publie son livre, le projet de film apparaît presque naturellement. « Fellipe voulait en faire un film, et notre collaboration s’est faite vraiment naturellement. C’est basé d’abord sur une amitié », résume Othmane Zine. Deux regards pour une même histoire Si Fellipe Barbosa porte avec lui le souvenir de son amie et une relation profondément personnelle à la famille, Othmane Zine représente une autre proximité : celle d’un Marocain qui a grandi avec Leïla, connaît sa famille et partage avec elle une partie de son environnement culturel. Cette double appartenance était, pour lui, essentielle à l’équilibre du film. « C’étaient deux regards qui se complétaient » , explique-t-il. Si Barbosa connaît très bien le Maroc, son regard reste celui d’un cinéaste brésilien vivant à l’étranger, issu d’une culture différente. Or le film traverse des questions liées à la religion, à l’islam et à la société marocaine. Zine a donc apporté ce que son parcours et sa proximité avec la famille lui permettaient de comprendre de l’intérieur. En retour, Barbosa a apporté son propre regard, extérieur et complémentaire. « La combinaison des deux fait que voilà, ça a apporté quelque chose de spécial à ce film », estime le réalisateur. C’est probablement l’un des choix fondamentaux du film. Le spectateur qui s’attendrait à découvrir la trajectoire de la photographe, son parcours professionnel ou les différentes étapes de sa vie peut être surpris. Othmane Zine tient à le préciser : « Il ne faut pas se tromper parce que ce n’est pas du tout un biopic. » Le film ne cherche donc pas à retracer la vie de Leïla Alaoui. Il s’intéresse à ce qui se passe après. À l’espace laissé vide par sa disparition. À la manière dont une famille tente de continuer à vivre lorsque l’un de ses membres disparaît brutalement. Le point de départ reste le livre écrit par son père, Aziz Alaoui. Les cinéastes ont voulu rester au plus près de sa vision et de son expérience. « Ce n’est pas un film sur Leïla : c’est un film qui parle de la perte de Leïla à travers les yeux de ses parents », souligne Zine. Cette nuance est essentielle. Le personnage absent devient le centre d’une histoire qui parle finalement de ceux qui restent : des parents, d’un couple, des frères et sœurs et des liens familiaux bouleversés par le deuil. Tourner dans la maison de Leïla à Marrakech Dans la ville ocre, le tournage a pris une dimension particulière. Une grande partie du film a été tournée dans la véritable maison familiale des Alaoui, là où Leïla a grandi. Pour Zine, ce choix a immédiatement changé l’atmosphère du plateau. « Le fait d’avoir tourné dans la vraie maison des Alaoui, tout de suite on se connecte avec Leïla qui a vécu dans cette maison, qui a grandi dans cette maison » , confie-t-il. La famille était également présente au quotidien pendant le tournage. Cette proximité a créé une forme de silence et de respect partagé par toute l’équipe. « Il y avait vraiment cette espèce de calme sur le plateau » , se souvient le réalisateur. Cette proximité avec la famille a également influencé le travail des comédiens. Pour Zine, les acteurs ne jouaient pas dans un environnement totalement fictif : ils étaient quotidiennement confrontés aux véritables personnes qui avaient vécu cette histoire. « Les acteurs aussi se nourrissaient du fait d’être quotidiennement avec les personnages qu’ils interprétaient », explique-t-il. La frontière entre fiction et réalité devenait ainsi particulièrement fine. Sans transformer le tournage en reconstitution documentaire, la présence de la famille apportait aux comédiens une matière humaine impossible à reproduire artificiellement. C’est aussi ce qui donne au film cette sensation d’intimité, sans que celle-ci ne devienne intrusive. Préserver la femme derrière la tragédie Au-delà du deuil, une autre exigence traverse le film : ne pas réduire Leïla à son statut de victime. Pour Othmane Zine, cette question était fondamentale. Parce que lui-même la connaissait, mais aussi parce que la tragédie pouvait facilement prendre toute la place. « Ce sont des sujets très graves, très douloureux, qu’il faut traiter avec pudeur » , affirme-t-il. La volonté était donc de préserver la femme derrière le drame, sans nier ce qui lui est arrivé. Le film part d’une tragédie profondément intime, mais cherche progressivement à lui donner une portée plus universelle. « Elle était une victime, certes, mais si on ouvre, le sujet est beaucoup plus vaste et beaucoup plus universel » , estime le réalisateur. C’est finalement dans cette tension entre proximité et distance que se situe le regard d’Othmane Zine. Lui qui a connu Leïla depuis l’enfance aurait pu choisir de raconter celle qu’il connaissait, ses souvenirs, son parcours, sa personnalité. Avec Fellipe Barbosa, il a fait un autre choix : raconter ce que sa disparition a produit autour d’elle. Un film sur l’absence plutôt qu’un portrait. Sur la famille plutôt que sur la carrière. Sur le deuil plutôt que sur la tragédie elle-même. Et peut-être est-ce précisément cette approche qui permet à « Leïla et la nuit » de dépasser l’histoire personnelle de Leïla Alaoui. En partant d’une famille et d’une perte profondément réelles, le film cherche finalement à parler d’une expérience que chacun peut reconnaître : celle de devoir apprendre à vivre avec l’absence. The post FIFM : Othmane Zine, le regard marocain derrière « Leïla et la nuit » appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Why G5 didn’t align with Obi, Atiku in 2023 — Makinde
items.description: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has explained why the G5 governors of the Peoples Democratic Party did not support the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, or align with Peter Obi of the Labour Party during the 2023 general election. Makinde said the governors, who opposed Atiku’s emergence as the PDP candidate, were dissatisfied with the party’s decision to abandon its zoning arrangement and leave the presidential ticket open. He said they had also approached both Atiku and Obi to discuss their expectations for governance beyond the 2023 election but did not reach an agreement with them. The governor spoke in an interview on the WithChude Podcast, where he recounted the events that led to the G5 governors breaking ranks with the PDP and eventually supporting President Bola Tinubu, then the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress. Makinde said he had championed the zoning of the PDP presidential ticket to the South after eight years of President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration, which was led by a northerner. “If you look at 2023, we had an issue in the PDP. I was at the forefront of zoning the presidency to the South in the PDP, such that after eight years of President Buhari, who’s from the North, you can have a southern president,” he said. However, he said the party’s decision to leave the zoning arrangement open paved the way for Atiku, a former vice-president from the North-East, to emerge as its presidential candidate. Makinde said the G5 governors subsequently approached Atiku and demanded certain changes to the party’s leadership and campaign structure to ensure that the South was adequately represented. He argued that having Atiku as the presidential candidate, Senator Iyorchia Ayu as national chairman from the North-Central and Governor Aminu Tambuwal as director-general of the campaign placed key decisions in the hands of three northern politicians. “Now you are the candidate of the party, there are certain things we want you to do. First is, you cannot be the candidate from the North-East. The national chairman of the party is Senator Ayu from the North-Central, and you’re appointing Governor Tambuwal as the DG of the campaign. “I mean, it’s the three of you that will sit and decide most things. And when you transition to government, it’s almost the same thing. So, what do we have to use to campaign for our own people in the South? So we couldn’t have an alignment,” he said. The governor said the disagreement forced the G5 governors to consider alternatives beyond the PDP and the immediate contest for the presidency. He said they approached both Obi, who was the Labour Party’s presidential candidate, and Tinubu to discuss the possibility of forming a government of national unity after the election. “So, we decided. Are there other options available to us? Yes, we started thinking about governance beyond the 2023 election. If you have to break rank across party lines, then you have to really go deep into governance, into what will happen after the election itself,” Makinde said. According to him, the discussions centred on building a country where no group would feel marginalised and where governance would serve all Nigerians rather than a privileged few. He said the governors had a fruitful discussion with Obi but were not convinced that their proposals would be implemented if he became president. “We approached Peter Obi. We approached Asiwaju, and we said, ‘Look, beyond this election, it will be a government of national unity. Nobody should be a slave in their own country. A Nigeria that will work for not just the privileged few, but everybody.’ “Those things were brought to the forefront, and then Peter Obi, we had a good discussion, but we didn’t get the feel that this will happen,” he said. Makinde said Tinubu, on the other hand, accepted their proposal for a government of national unity, alongside other principles they had presented, including national competence. He added that the decision to support the ruling party was also influenced by the need to ensure that their political gamble did not end in failure after they had broken ranks with their party. “So, when we now approached the president, and we brought this before him, he accepted government of national unity, all of those things we have put together, national competence, and things like that,” he said. The governor said the G5 governors believed there was little room for failure after deciding to go against their party, making it necessary to choose an option they considered more likely to deliver on their expectations. items.title: Assin Central cocoa farmers accuse gov’t of supplying expired fertiliser, overpricing
items.description: Some cocoa farmers in Assin Central in the Central Region have accused the government of supplying them with expired liquid fertiliser and charging GH¢5 per bottle, despite the product being intended for free distribution. The farmers, through their Member of Parliament, Reverend John Ntim Fordjour, allege that the fertiliser supplied to them had expired in February 2026, raising concerns about the quality of agricultural inputs being distributed to cocoa farmers. Speaking on JoyNews’ AM Show , the MP said about 10 farmers had brought the matter to his attention and provided videos showing what he described as evidence of tampered labels on the fertiliser bottles. He alleged that the original expiry dates had been concealed with replacement labels, making it difficult for farmers to establish the products’ actual expiry dates. Reverend Ntim Fordjour further claimed that “they even took money, GH¢5 per bottle, when it’s been imprinted on the bottle that not for sale. They still took, collected, extorted five cedis per bottle from each farmer,” he said. He has called on COCOBOD and the Ministry of Agriculture to investigate the allegations and establish how the products were distributed to the farmers. However, COCOBOD has rejected the MP’s characterisation of the matter, describing his claims as distorted. Its Head of Public Affairs, Jerome Kwame Sam, said the Board had opened an investigation but criticised the MP for suggesting that COCOBOD was deliberately distributing expired fertiliser. “For a Member of Parliament to come out and then make a generic statement as to COCOBOD is deliberately distributing expired fertiliser is very unfortunate,” he said. Mr Sam explained that the disputed products formed part of a 2024 contract awarded by the previous COCOBOD administration for the supply of approximately 143,000 litres of natural foliar fertiliser. He said the products were delivered in 2025 and that COCOBOD subsequently conducted a physical verification exercise in May that year to determine whether the consignment met the specifications agreed under the contract. According to him, the verification team identified a discrepancy in the product description, with the word ‘neutral’ appearing instead of ‘natural’. He said the supplier was alerted to the discrepancy and asked to address it. COCOBOD says investigations into the allegations are ongoing.

items.title: Saraki cautions Kwara Gov over treatment of traditional rulers
items.description: Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has urged Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq to respect traditional rulers and allow them receive political leaders across party lines. Saraki made the call following allegations that the governor had summoned some traditional rulers to Ilorin and threatened to suspend those who received leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during courtesy visits to their palaces. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki said the alleged actions followed his stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District, which began last week. He explained that visits to traditional rulers were part of established customs and protocols, adding that the royal fathers should be allowed to receive political leaders regardless of their party affiliations. Saraki said traditional rulers were fathers of all and should not be subjected to pressure over their interactions with politicians. He also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to caution Abdulrazaq, saying political differences should not prevent opposition parties from engaging communities and traditional institutions. The former Senate President recalled that during the 16 years the PDP governed Kwara State, traditional rulers were not prevented from receiving opposition leaders. He said democracy required tolerance of opposing views and urged the governor to respect the state’s traditional institutions. Saraki, however, insisted that the alleged actions would not discourage the PDP from continuing its engagements across the state. He said the party would sustain its outreach to communities in the three senatorial districts, adding that the response to its engagements had been encouraging. Saraki Accuses Kwara Governor of Intimidating Traditional Rulers Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has cautioned Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq against allegedly threatening and intimidating traditional rulers over their reception of leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during campaign visits. Saraki also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to call the governor to order, saying his alleged conduct was inconsistent with the democratic principles of the party. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki alleged that since he began stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District last week, Abdulrazaq had been summoning traditional rulers to Ilorin or threatening to suspend those who received his delegation on courtesy visits to their palaces. He described the alleged actions as unacceptable, insisting that traditional rulers were fathers of all and should not be drawn into partisan politics. “Since I commenced my stakeholder engagement in the Kwara North Senatorial District last week, Mr Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq has been summoning traditional rulers in the district to Ilorin or threatening to suspend those who receive our delegation on a courtesy visit. This is unacceptable because we are in a democracy, and traditional rulers, as fathers of all, are not politicians,” he said. Saraki explained that courtesy visits to traditional rulers were part of established customs and traditional protocols, particularly when political delegations visited their domains to engage stakeholders. He said it would amount to a breach of traditional protocol for political leaders to hold meetings with community stakeholders without first informing the royal fathers. The former Senate President accused the governor of using threatening telephone calls, official summons and messages to pressure traditional rulers who received the PDP delegation. “We consider it distasteful, disrespectful, dictatorial, and uncivilised for the governor to be making threatening phone calls, issuing official summons, and sending coercive messages to the royal fathers because they received and listened to us,” he said. Saraki questioned why the courtesy visits should be considered a threat to the governor’s political interests, adding that the alleged actions could undermine the state’s traditional institutions. He recalled that during the 16 years the PDP governed Kwara State, traditional rulers were not prevented or punished for receiving opposition leaders. According to him, democracy should allow competing political ideas to reach the electorate without intimidation or suppression of opposing views. He described the alleged conduct as a departure from democratic principles and compared it to practices associated with military rule. Saraki further called on Abdulrazaq, who is also the chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF), to demonstrate democratic leadership and respect for traditional institutions. He said the governor’s alleged actions would not deter the PDP from taking its campaign messages to communities across the state. “We do not know what his fears are, but he should know that his antics will not deter the PDP from taking its messages to all the nooks and crannies of the state,” Saraki said. He added that the response to the party’s engagements across the three senatorial districts had encouraged its members to continue their outreach. items.title: Bolt urges shared responsibility for road safety, calls on drivers and passengers to use safety features
items.description: Bolt Ghana has called for greater collaboration among road safety stakeholders, urging regulators, ride-hailing companies, drivers and passengers to take collective responsibility for reducing road accidents. The company says addressing road safety challenges requires more than regulations, stressing the need for public education and the effective use of safety measures available to road users. Senior Operations Manager at Bolt Ghana, Jonathan Ahumah-Sackey, said road accidents have far-reaching consequences for families and the economy, making safety a critical priority for all stakeholders. Speaking on road safety, he noted that every road accident statistic represents a person whose death or injury affects families, dependants and livelihoods. “Each number in that statistic is someone’s family member. It could be somebody’s brother, it could be a mother, father, or breadwinner, and it affects families,” he said. He explained that Bolt considers safety a central part of its operations and has integrated several features into its ride-hailing application to help protect both drivers and passengers. Mr Ahumah-Sackey said road safety is a shared responsibility involving regulators, service providers, drivers and passengers, with each group expected to play a distinct role. He said regulators must establish and enforce the necessary laws and standards, while ride-hailing companies must provide the technology and tools to support safer journeys. Drivers, he added, must comply with road traffic regulations and make responsible decisions behind the wheel, while passengers must familiarise themselves with available safety features and use them when necessary. Safety measures before, during and after trips Mr Ahumah-Sackey said Bolt’s safety approach covers every stage of a journey, beginning with checks before a trip. He encouraged passengers to verify that the vehicle arriving to pick them up matches the details displayed on the application before boarding. During trips, he said passengers and drivers can access several safety features, including audio recording, trip-sharing and an emergency assistance function. He explained that these measures are intended to give users additional protection and provide avenues for reporting concerns. After each trip, Bolt collects feedback from both drivers and passengers, which contributes to their respective ratings. The company also investigates safety incidents reported during trips to help address concerns and improve its services. He noted that ride-hailing platforms play an important role in building trust between drivers and passengers who may otherwise be strangers to one another. According to him, the platforms help passengers identify their drivers and vehicles while providing a system through which driver requirements and verification processes can be monitored. Bolt cautions against prioritising speed over safety On the growing use of delivery services, Mr Ahumah-Sackey cautioned drivers against allowing pressure to meet delivery timelines to compromise road safety. Using the delivery of medication as an example, he said companies and drivers must strike a balance between timely delivery and the safety of riders. He explained that an accident could injure the rider while also preventing the intended recipient from receiving essential medication. He therefore urged drivers to observe traffic regulations and avoid speeding or taking unnecessary risks to complete trips and deliveries quickly. Calls for stronger safety education Mr Ahumah-Sackey identified public education as critical to making road safety interventions effective. He said the availability of safety features alone would not guarantee protection if drivers and passengers were unaware of them or did not understand how to use them. “The safety tools exist. But if we don’t know that they exist and we don’t know how to use them, then they become ineffective,” he said. He called for stronger education by regulators and ride-hailing companies, adding that collaboration among industry players could help expand public awareness and encourage the effective use of available safety measures. He believes a coordinated approach, supported by education and responsible behaviour, will be essential to improving safety on Ghana’s roads.

items.description: Kara, 25 nov. (ATOP) – Cinq établissements scolaires des inspections de l’enseignement secondaire général (IESG) de Bassar et Niamtougou dans la région de la Kara, ont bénéficié du matériel informatique et des mallettes scientifiques, offerts par le Fonds des Nations Unies pour l’Enfance (UNICEF). La cérémonie de remise officielle a eu lieu le mardi 24 novembre à la direction régionale de l’Education de la Kara. Estimé à plus de 80.000.000 FCFA, cet équipement est destiné aux Collèges d’enseignement général (CEG) Nawaré et Guérin-kouka 1 et le lycée Guérin-kouka 2, dans l’IESG Bassar, et les lycées Kantè ville 2 et Ossacré dans l’IESG Niamtougou. Le don contribuera à améliorer la qualité des enseignements et des apprentissages au profit de 7300 bénéficiaires directs dont 3.000 filles des établissements bénéficiaires. Il s’agit également de renforcer l’engagement des autorités éducatives et chefs d’établissement en faveur de l’intégration des outils informatiques et scientifiques dans les pratiques pédagogiques, puis de valoriser le partenariat entre l’institution onusienne, les autorités nationales et les acteurs du système éducatif. Le secrétaire général du Conseil régional de la Kara, Esso Pirénéwè, a salué le geste de l’UNICEF, précisant que l’importance de l’outil informatique dans l’éducation des apprenants, n’est plus à démontrer. Il a exhorté les bénéficiaires à en faire bon usage pour une valeur ajoutée dans leurs études. Pour Mme Erinna Dia, représentante résidente de l’UNICEF au Togo, ce matériel est le fruit du partenariat de longue date entre le Togo et son institution. Elle a insisté sur l’importance de l’éducation de la jeune fille, estimant que cet équipement est censé renforcer les connaissances chez elle ci. En réceptionnant le don au nom du ministre de l’Education nationale, le directeur régional de l’Education de la Kara, Badjaglana Fontou Bograh, a souligné que l’initiative vient à point nommé renforcer les efforts déjà consentis par les autorités nationales, faisant de l’éducation un des piliers du développement local, via une digitalisation maîtrisée du système éducatif. Il a exprimé sa gratitude à l’UNICEF pour son accompagnement et aux autorités pour leur engagement en faveur d’une éducation de qualité. Au nom des bénéficiaires, M. Kokou Kossou, chef de l’IESG-Niamtougou a remercié la généreuse donatrice, lui promettant de veiller à la bonne utilisation du matériel dans l’intérêt supérieur des apprenants. ATOP/LER/TAL/BA

items.title: 58% of Nigerian women who suffer violence remain silent – Survey
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – NEARLY six in 10 Nigerian women who have experienced physical or sexual violence have neither sought help nor disclosed their ordeal to anyone, highlighting the widespread silence and barriers to justice confronting survivors of gender-based violence in the country. The 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) revealed that 58 per cent of women aged 15 to 49 who experienced physical or sexual violence neither sought help nor told anyone about their experiences. The survey also showed that 21 per cent of women within the age group had experienced physical or sexual violence. The findings have renewed calls for stronger protection mechanisms, improved access to justice and greater accountability for perpetrators, with gender-based violence advocates warning that legal reforms and public awareness campaigns alone would not end the problem without changes in societal attitudes and institutional practices. Speaking at a screening of ‘Sanctuary’, a film by Chavala Yaduma, organised by the Public and Private Development Centre (PPDC) under its HomeVida film-for-change initiative to mark the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, the Head of Communications and Knowledge Management at PPDC, Nnenna Eze, identified stigma, victim-blaming, disbelief and the lack of safe spaces as major reasons survivors remained silent. Eze said gender-based violence occurred in different settings, including homes, schools, workplaces, intimate relationships and online spaces, stressing that addressing the problem required more than public declarations and awareness campaigns. She also expressed concern over the low rate of legal accountability for reported cases, citing figures released by the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development in June 2026. “In June 2026, the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development said that 2,755 cases of gender-based and intimate partner violence had been recorded between January and April. The Ministry also said that only 4% had reached legal accountability, which is a very low rate, if you would agree with me. Those figures were published by the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation”, she said. Also speaking, a gender-based violence expert, Hassana Maina, called for urgent reforms to Nigeria’s legal system, warning that outdated laws, discriminatory beliefs and institutional failures continued to undermine justice for survivors. Maina insisted that sexual violence must be treated strictly as a crime, arguing that Nigeria needed to move beyond colonial-era legal practices and address the societal attitudes that continued to excuse abuse. On the Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act, she said that although efforts had been made to secure its adoption and implementation across states, passing legislation alone was insufficient without addressing the institutional structures and societal beliefs that weakened its enforcement. She said, “We need to broaden our understanding of what justice should look like. Yes, sexual violence is a criminal offence, and the state is responsible for prosecuting perpetrators. But what happens when the state itself does not fully recognise violence against women as a crime? “There are people within our institutions who still hold on to the belief that women’s bodies are freely accessible, or that marriage can somehow erase the wrongdoing of sexual violence. These attitudes undermine justice and reinforce the culture of impunity.” She also stressed that the responsibility for tackling gender-based violence could not rest on survivors or individuals alone, adding that the legal system, institutional practices and societal beliefs that perpetuated abuse must also be addressed. Similarly, PPDC’s Programmes and Research Officer, HomeVida Media and Films, Abdulmuizz Oyekola, called for stronger government action to protect survivors, improve access to justice and ensure the prosecution of perpetrators. Oyekola urged the government to strengthen institutions responsible for addressing gender-based violence, particularly the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), and provide them with adequate resources and institutional support to discharge their responsibilities effectively. He also called for improved protection mechanisms, recovery services and support systems for survivors, noting that boys, alongside women and girls, could also experience abuse and should be covered by government interventions. He explained that PPDC used films and other cultural platforms to promote behavioural change by exposing audiences to survivors’ experiences and encouraging conversations around issues often ignored or normalised in society. According to him, the screening brought together stakeholders in the gender-based violence sector to examine existing challenges and explore ways of strengthening collective efforts to address the problem. The film, ‘Sanctuary’, portrays a girl allegedly sexually abused by a religious leader and her struggle to find help, highlighting the need for supportive environments where survivors can speak out and access justice rather than suffer in silence. The 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence is being observed this year under the theme, ‘UNiTE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity’. items.title: Al Barid Bank et l’AMSD s’associent pour soutenir le don de sang
items.description: Al Barid Bank et l’Agence Marocaine du Sang et de ses Dérivés (AMSD) ont signé, au siège d’Al Barid Bank à Casablanca, une convention-cadre de partenariat d’une durée de trois ans visant à promouvoir le don de sang volontaire, bénévole et régulier. Signée par Al-Amine Nejjar, Président du Directoire d’Al Barid Bank, et le Pr Kamal Doghmi, Directeur de l’AMSD, cette convention s’appuie sur le réseau de proximité de la banque pour soutenir les actions de sensibilisation et faciliter l’organisation de collectes dans les territoires. Ce partenariat conjugue la mission de service public de l’AMSD, chargée de garantir la disponibilité et la sécurité des produits sanguins sur l’ensemble du territoire national, et l’engagement sociétal d’Al Barid Bank, qui met sa proximité au service de cette cause d’intérêt général. Dans ce cadre, Al Barid Bank sensibilisera ses collaborateurs à l’importance du don régulier et encouragera leur participation, sur une base strictement volontaire. La banque pourra également apporter un appui logistique pour mener à bien les campagnes organisées par l’AMSD dans les territoires. Grâce à ses relais régionaux, Al Barid Bank contribuera également à diffuser les messagesde sensibilisation au don de sang, notamment dans les zones rurales ou éloignées. Uncomitéde suivi réunissant les deux partenaires évaluera les actions menées et leur déploiement territorial. The post Al Barid Bank et l’AMSD s’associent pour soutenir le don de sang appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Adeleke dissolves cabinet, retains SSG, CoS, spokesperson
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Ahead of his second-term inauguration, Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has dissolved the State Executive Council, thanking members for their contributions to the development of the state. However, the governor retained the Secretary to the State Government (SSG), Teslim Igbalaye; Chief of Staff, Kazeem Akinleye; and his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed. A statement issued by Rasheed after the valedictory Executive Council meeting on Wednesday said Adeleke reflected on the administration’s achievements since 2023 and commended members for their contributions. The governor said the administration had recorded achievements in education, health, sports, infrastructure, science and technology, digital economy and climate change, among other sectors. He said: “For almost four years, we jointly ran our dear state with several accomplishments and achievements. “Our team succeeded on several fronts where the previous administration failed. We delivered successfully in education, health, sports, infrastructure, science and tech, digital economy, climate change and several others. We got several awards from local and national bodies for our uncommon achievements.” Adeleke expressed appreciation to members of the council for their service, saying they had conducted themselves with honour and integrity in their respective ministries and areas of responsibility. “On behalf of the people and government of Osun State, I extend our sincere commendation to all council members. We will not forget all those who are part of this golden era in the history of Osun development. “It is on this note that I hereby dissolve the Osun State Executive Council. All political appointees are equally relieved of their appointments,” he said. The governor, however, exempted the SSG, Chief of Staff and his spokesperson from the dissolution. He also announced that the Local Government Service Commission and the recently reconstituted board of Osun State University would remain undissolved. The statement directed all affected political appointees to hand over to directors or permanent secretaries in their respective ministries. items.title: Météo-Tunisie | Des pluies orageuses attendues cette nuit
items.description: Le temps s'annonce contrasté cette nuit en Tunisie, selon l’Institut national de la météorologie (INM) qui prévoit des passages nuageux parfois abondants avec des pluies éparses sur le nord, tandis que le ciel restera partiellement voilé sur le reste du territoire. Dans son bulletin, l'INM précise que les averses seront temporairement orageuses et localement soutenues dans l'extrême nord-ouest, notamment du côté de Tabarka dans le gouvernorat de Jendouba, ajoutant que les vents seront assez forts à forts près des côtes avec des rafales dépassant 70 km/h sous orages. Côté températures, les nocturnes seront comprise entre 15°C et 19°C avec une fraîcheur plus marquée sur les hauteurs, avec des minimales à 10°C. Y. N . items.title: KP’s Karak reports 'first polio case in 6 years', taking countrywide 2026 tally to 10
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication (NEOC) has confirmed the country’s 10th paralytic polio case of the year, with the latest infection from Karak district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. According to an official of the polio programme, the affected child is a 14-month-old girl from the district’s Shnawa Gudi Khel union council. The case is the first reported from Karak in six years, and the eighth of the year from KP, according to NEOC. “The case is genetically linked to poliovirus detected in southern KP, where poliovirus circulation has remained intense this year despite an overall transmission reduction in the country,” the official said. The centre underscored the urgency of consistent vaccination across the country to keep all children protected from lifelong paralysis. According to the official, Bannu district — which borders Karak — has reported wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) in sewage samples for the past eight months, which means that continued virus circulation remains a major risk to children’s wellbeing. The country’s ninth polio case of the year was reported earlier this month, in KP’s Khyber district. Of the 10 cases reported this year, eight have been reported from KP and two from Sindh. Pakistan is one of the last two countries in the world, alongside Afghanistan, where polio remains endemic. Polio has no cure and can cause lifelong paralysis or even death. It is therefore essential that every child under five receives two drops of the oral polio vaccine during each vaccination campaign. The vaccine is prequalified by the World Health Organisation (WHO) and has been safely used in 195 countries, including all Muslim-majority countries. With the help of the vaccine and the efforts of hundreds of thousands of polio workers, Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8pc since the launch of its national eradication programme in 1994. The number of cases has fallen from an estimated 20,000 to 31 in 2025 . The third sub-national polio vaccination campaign of 2026, targeting 97 high-risk districts across the country, was launched in October by the Pakistan Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI). The drive was part of intensified efforts to stop poliovirus transmission and protect children from lifelong paralysis.

items.title: GIHOC targets return to market leadership in Ghana, expansion across West Africa – CEO
items.description: The Ghana Industrial Holding Company (GIHOC) Distilleries Company Limited says it is committed to restoring its position as a leading alcoholic beverage manufacturer in Ghana and expanding its market presence across West Africa. Chief Executive Officer of GIHOC, Jones Bortey Applerh, says management is pursuing a strategy to reposition the company through improved staff welfare, quality production and stronger corporate development. He made the remarks while expressing appreciation to the company’s board for supporting the acquisition of new buses to improve staff transportation. According to him, the buses represent part of a broader effort to rebuild the company and restore its reputation as one of Ghana’s longstanding industrial establishments. “Those of us in management and the staff, we are committed to building a first-class distillery. We are committed to restoring GIHOC to its former glory,” he said. Mr Applerh stressed that staff welfare remains central to the company’s growth strategy, noting that a motivated workforce is critical to achieving its corporate objectives. He said management wants to build an organisation that respects workers’ rights and provides an environment where employees feel valued and supported. The CEO added that GIHOC is focused on producing quality products that Ghanaians can take pride in while working towards regaining its market share in the alcoholic beverage industry. He further assured the board and other stakeholders that the newly acquired buses would be properly maintained and used for their intended purpose. Mr. Applerh said management remains committed to building a sustainable institution that future generations of Ghanaians will be proud of.

items.title: Gestion de la performance sportive : Le cabinet Rodel organise un forum du 1er au 5 décembre à Ouagadougou
items.description: Le Forum Sport et Développement Durable se tiendra du 1er au 5 décembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, autour du thème « La gestion de la performance dans le sport : enjeux et défis ». L’événement, annoncé lors d’une conférence de presse ce 25 novembre au Stade du 4-Août, entend renforcer les capacités des acteurs sportifs et rapprocher les connaissances scientifiques des pratiques de terrain. Organisé par le cabinet Rodel, le forum se déroulera en deux étapes. Les 1er et 2 décembre, les échanges auront lieu dans la salle polyvalente du Centre international de conférences de Ouaga 2000. Les 3 et 4 décembre seront consacrés à des formations au Stade du 4-Août. Pour Alexandre Le Grand Rouamba, président du comité d’organisation, le choix du thème répond aux exigences actuelles du sport de haut niveau. « Le talent brut, bien qu’indispensable, ne suffit plus pour hisser nos athlètes et nos équipes sur les plus hautes marches des podiums internationaux. La performance ne s’improvise plus. Elle se planifie, se mesure, s’analyse et se gère avec rigueur » , a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, la préparation physique et mentale, le suivi médical, la nutrition, l’analyse des données et la gouvernance des structures sportives sont autant de facteurs qui influencent les résultats des athlètes. Réduire l’écart entre potentiel et exigences du haut niveau Le comité d’organisation ambitionne de contribuer à combler le fossé entre le potentiel des sportifs burkinabè et les exigences de la compétition internationale. Il s’agit notamment de mettre à la disposition des fédérations, des clubs, des entraîneurs et des encadreurs techniques des outils méthodologiques et scientifiques adaptés. « Il s'agit de doter nos fédérations, nos clubs, nos entraîneurs et nos encadreurs techniques des outils méthodologiques et scientifiques les plus récents pour optimiser le rendement de nos athlètes tout en préservant leur santé et leur intégrité » , a expliqué Alexandre Le Grand Rouamba. Durant les cinq jours, les participants pourront prendre part à des panels, des master class et des échanges d’expériences avec des spécialistes nationaux et étrangers, d’anciens champions et des gestionnaires de structures sportives. Les thématiques annoncées portent notamment sur la gouvernance des organisations sportives, la détection et la formation des talents, la récupération, la préparation psychologique et mentale, la nutrition, l’utilisation des nouvelles technologies ainsi que l’impact du changement climatique sur les infrastructures sportives. Le président du comité d’organisation a également appelé les acteurs du sport à s’approprier cette rencontre. « Aux acteurs du monde sportif, ce forum est le vôtre. Saisissez cette opportunité unique pour questionner vos pratiques et franchir un nouveau cap » , a-t-il lancé. Un projet qui entend se poursuivre après le forum-©Faso7 Pour Edgar Lelo, Directeur général du cabinet Rodel et porteur de l’événement, cette initiative s’inscrit dans une démarche d’accompagnement du secteur sportif burkinabè. Le cabinet, qui intervient notamment dans le conseil aux entreprises et la gestion de projets, affirme s’intéresser depuis plusieurs années aux questions de jeunesse et de sport. Il a rappelé que le cabinet avait participé à l’élaboration du premier document de politique nationale de la jeunesse et formulé des propositions ayant contribué à la création d’un espace de proximité destiné à la pratique du sport et des loisirs. « Pour le cabinet Rodel, on ne fait pas le forum pour faire un forum. […] Pour cette édition, nous sommes dans la même dynamique : faire un forum, mais suivre derrière par un projet qu’on va proposer aux autorités » , a-t-il indiqué, exprimant l’espoir que cette proposition puisse être retenue. Le choix de la performance comme thème central découle, selon Edgar Lelo, des enjeux de compétitivité du sport. Il estime que cette notion ne concerne pas uniquement les athlètes déjà au sommet, mais l’ensemble du parcours qui conduit un jeune sportif vers le haut niveau. « Nous partons de zéro à amener quelqu’un sur le podium. Et c’est tout ce processus que nous voulons [aborder] dans ce forum à travers les panels qui sont proposés » , a-t-il expliqué. La gouvernance et la formation au cœur du parcours Le directeur général de Rodel a souligné que la performance dépend d’abord de la gouvernance des structures sportives. Les décisions prises au niveau des bureaux fédéraux et des clubs influencent, selon lui, les conditions de préparation et les résultats obtenus sur le terrain. La détection et la formation des jeunes constituent un autre déterminant. « Si vous avez mal détecté les jeunes, vous ne pouvez pas forcément produire un champion » , a-t-il relevé. Les échanges porteront également sur le suivi mental, psychologique et nutritionnel des sportifs, ainsi que sur l’apport des nouvelles technologies, notamment l’intelligence artificielle et les données dans l’accompagnement des athlètes. L’impact du changement climatique sur les infrastructures sportives figure aussi au programme. À travers ces différents axes, les organisateurs souhaitent faire de la performance une démarche structurée, depuis la détection des talents jusqu’à leur accompagnement vers les compétitions de haut niveau. Le Forum Sport et Développement Durable se veut ainsi un cadre de partage entre les institutions sportives, les scientifiques, le secteur privé et les médias, avec l’ambition de contribuer à une gestion plus méthodique et durable de la performance au Burkina Faso. Josué TIENDREBEOGO Faso7 L’article Gestion de la performance sportive : Le cabinet Rodel organise un forum du 1er au 5 décembre à Ouagadougou est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Sécurité routière : Un appel à la responsabilité collective reiteré
items.description: La Journée mondiale du souvenir des victimes des accidents de la route a été célébrée, le 24 novembre à travers une cérémonie d’hommage et de recueillement. L’occasion de rendre hommage aux personnes disparues, de témoigner de la solidarité aux familles endeuillées et de renouveler l’engagement en faveur de la prévention routière. La rencontre de cette année a été marquée par la présence de la Première Dame, Absa Faye, désignée Ambassadrice de la Sécurité routière. À travers cette mission, elle porte le plaidoyer en faveur de « routes plus sûres et d'une mobilité responsable pour tous », soulignent les services de communication de l’'Agence Nationale de la Sécurité Routière (ANASER). La cérémonie a également enregistré la participation du Directeur de Cabinet du ministre des Transports terrestres et aériens. Sa présence traduit, selon de l’ANASER organisatrice, «l'engagement des autorités à renforcer les actions de prévention et à promouvoir une culture de sécurité routière ». Au-delà de l’hommage rendu aux victimes, cette journée a permis de rappeler l’ampleur de la responsabilité collective face à l’insécurité routière. « Chaque vie compte », rappelle la note. Les responsables de la structure appellent dès lors les usagers à «redoubler d'efforts pour prévenir les accidents, protéger les usagers de la route et sauver des vies».

items.title: Senate Appropriations Committee session turns violent as aide, security operatives clash
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — A legislative aide to Senator Allwell Onyesoh (Rivers East) was allegedly assaulted by security operatives attached to the Senate Committee on Appropriations, chaired by Senator Olamilekan Adeola (APC, Ogun West), during a confrontation at the National Assembly complex, Abuja. The aide, Barrister Kingsley Wali, reportedly sustained head injuries during the incident and was rushed to the National Assembly Clinic for medical attention. Wali alleged that he and another aide to Senator Onyesoh, identified as Dr Kingsley, were attacked by security personnel after accompanying their principal to an Appropriations Committee meeting. Recounting the incident, Wali said the confrontation occurred after Senator Onyesoh had entered the committee room and he attempted to follow him. He said security personnel at the entrance were trying to close the door and stopped him from entering. According to him, when the operatives attempted to push his colleague away, he explained that their principal had already entered the room and that they were not attempting to force their way inside. He alleged that the situation escalated when the security personnel grabbed Dr Kingsley by the neck and began assaulting him. “I kept telling them to leave him alone because he is our senator’s personal assistant and my colleague. I even held one of the security personnel’s hands and pleaded with him to stop beating him,” Wali said. He further alleged that the operatives turned on him because he intervened on behalf of his colleague. Wali claimed that one of the security personnel grabbed him and pushed him down a staircase, while three others allegedly cornered him and repeatedly hit his head with the butt of a gun. He said the assault continued until he slumped, after which the operatives left him. According to him, Dr Kingsley subsequently took photographs of his condition and sent them to Senator Onyesoh through WhatsApp while the senator was attending the committee meeting. Wali said the senator came out after receiving the photographs and found him lying in a pool of blood. He added that the senator subsequently took him into the committee room, where members expressed shock at his condition and directed that he be taken to the hospital for treatment. Speaking about his condition, Wali said he was still weak following the alleged assault and the fall. “I’m weak. I’m completely weak because they pushed me down and I slumped. But God will take care of everything. I thank God for everything,” he said. However, Senator Adeola’s Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Odunaro, offered a different account of the incident. In a statement titled, “Security Breach at Senate Committee on Appropriations Room,” Odunaro said the confrontation followed a misunderstanding between aides of some senators attempting to gain access to a committee room during a closed-door session and security personnel stationed at the entrance. He said the incident occurred without the knowledge of Adeola, who was already presiding over the meeting alongside members of the committee, including Senator Onyesoh. According to the statement, Adeola only became aware of the incident when Onyesoh briefly stepped out of the meeting and found his bloodied aide. Odunaro said the committee chairman directed the Clerk of the Committee to take the injured aide to the National Assembly Clinic, where he was treated and discharged. He added that the National Assembly management had commenced an investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the confrontation. “The incident is currently under investigation by the Management of the National Assembly to ascertain the facts that led to the ugly incident,” the statement said. The post Senate Appropriations Committee session turns violent as aide, security operatives clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Black Friday Is Becoming a Battle of the Bots
items.description: When Cynthia Bell McGillis needs help with her holiday shopping, she turns to Mrs. Claus. Not the one in the North Pole, but her own custom-built AI agent. After getting a head start on buying Christmas presents last month, McGillis had an idea of how to more easily keep track of her purchases: “I bet Grok can help with that,” McGillis, who works in marketing for an AI start-up in San Diego, told me. She instructed Grok Bot, an AI assistant made by Elon Musk, to constantly scan her email inbox every day. “Mrs. Claus” now logs arriving items and who they are for, searches the newsletters McGillis subscribes to for sales on potential gift ideas, and keeps a running total of how much McGillis has spent. The day we spoke, the bot had just surfaced a discount on Old Navy Christmas-themed pajamas. In recent months, tech companies have launched a number of AI personal assistants, one after the other. Instinct, an agent that allows users to chat with it directly from the iMessage app, went viral in August ; the next month, Meta launched its competitor, Muse. According to Mark Zuckerberg, more than 10 million users tried Muse in its first six weeks. Unlike traditional chatbots, AI agents can act on your behalf in the real world: Feed them your credit-card information and online passwords (if you dare), and they can find restaurant reservations, book flights, and, yes, buy gifts on your behalf. This month, OpenAI debuted ChatGPT Wallet, allowing its agents to also make purchases for users. [ Read: AI agents are here. Nobody’s ready. ] Now, for the first time, some people are about to open presents that were chosen and purchased entirely by bots. When Rohit Bakshi, an AI-product director in the Bay Area, wanted to get his nephew a Tin Can, the popular Wi-Fi-enabled “landline” for kids , he messaged Instinct to buy it. Bakshi told me that using Instinct more for holiday shopping would be a “no-brainer.” I heard similar enthusiasm from Boaz Sobrado, a tech worker also based in the Bay Area. (Every agentic-AI-loving shopper I could find had some connection to the tech industry.) Sobrado recently asked his girlfriend’s Muse agent, which knows her Instagram likes and saved posts, to find a hotel that matched her tastes. Agents can crawl through hundreds of text messages and emails to identify a tailored gift—something the intended recipient mentioned a long time ago, maybe, or something they might like based on contextual clues. AI companies are certainly invested in the notion that their personal assistants can be heroes this holiday season. In an email, Ben Schwerin, the chief business officer of Instinct, told me that the company has seen a recent uptick in people using its agents to shop. “What’s been interesting is people are trusting Instinct to complete purchases for a full gift list, rather than handing Instinct one-off links,” he said. Meanwhile, Meta is partnering with social-media influencers to tout how Muse can be used for holiday shopping, such as by choosing gifts on a budget. (Meta declined to answer questions about how people are using Muse for holiday shopping.) Americans without ties to the tech industry so far seem less bought in. AI assistants, for the most part, have yet to fully enter the mainstream. Some of that gap may be principled: Much of the country, after all, remains concerned about AI’s rapid development, and people certainly have good reason to be uncomfortable with the idea of a bot shopping with their credit card and having detailed access to their family’s personal information. AI assistants can also be expensive, many requiring subscriptions that run more than $100 a month. Some major retailers, including Amazon, have banned AI agents; the e-commerce giant is reportedly worried about what shopping bots could mean for its advertising business. Still, it may be only a matter of time. The promise of convenience can be hard to ignore. Lots of people who aren’t using agents to shop on their behalf are still asking AI for gift-giving help. This year, 40 percent of shoppers say they plan to use generative AI for holiday shopping, such as by asking ChatGPT for product recommendations, according to a recent report from Accenture. Kath Gramling, who leads the consumer-goods-and-retail division at Accenture, believes that many people who use LLMs may soon adopt AI agents too. “It’s just a natural extension,” Gramling told me. More shoppers may soon experience what can go wrong when you let an AI personal assistant run wild. One man claimed on X that his AI agent accidentally posted his bank-account balances in a Slack channel at his workplace; another man told Business Insider that a request for ingredients to make dinner for two resulted in a 20-pound chicken-wing order. Indeed, not all of Sobrado’s purchases have been successful: He recently ordered flowers for his girlfriend using his Muse agent, which he named Hermenegildo. When the flowers arrived, he realized that the agent had attached a card for his girlfriend and signed it, With love, Hermenegildo . [ Read: It’s all fun and games until you give AI your credit card ] Even if you aren’t using an AI personal assistant to buy any gifts, the bots might still affect your holiday-shopping experience. Last month, a Verge reporter wrote that she was able to instruct her Muse agent to continuously hold items in her cart on the RealReal, blocking other potential shoppers from purchasing them on the secondhand-luxury-fashion website. (Following the report, the RealReal said that the company would make it more difficult for agents to shop on its website.) And on Tuesday, Walmart announced that the company will now let Muse agents browse for deals and make purchases on users’ behalf. Black Fridays of decades past were an endurance game of who could wake up at the crack of dawn and brave the freezing weather in pursuit of a deal. This Black Friday might be a competition of who has the best AI agent. All of this raises the age-old holiday question: What is gift giving really for ? AI agents will never be able to replicate the experiential aspects of holiday magic. I love spending weeks clicking through websites until I feel the eureka moment of finding the perfect gift that I know someone will love. Others enjoy walking in a physical mall during the holidays, past the twinkling lights and smiling Santa. Bakshi told me that he can’t imagine letting Instinct do all of his holiday shopping. “I like going to the stores,” he said. “There’s a lot of festivity to it.” The principle stands that a Christmas gift is supposed to symbolize the love and appreciation you feel for a recipient. Instead, gift-giving frequently becomes a matter of commercialism and obligation. Now AI agents are opening the possibility of delivering incredibly personal gifts with about the same effort it takes to purchase a gift card. Hopefully for gift givers, they’ll get everyone’s name right.

items.title: Sûreté : Hammouchi valide 15 nouvelles nominations dans 7 villes du Royaume
items.description: La Direction générale de la sûreté nationale (DGSN) a annoncé, mercredi 25 novembre, une nouvelle série de nominations à des postes de responsabilité dans plusieurs services de police. Validées par le directeur général de la sûreté nationale, Abdellatif Hammouchi, ces désignations concernent 15 postes dans sept villes et portent notamment sur la sécurité publique et la police cynotechnique. La DGSN poursuit le renouvellement des responsables au sein de ses différentes structures territoriales. Une nouvelle vague de nominations a été annoncée mercredi, touchant les services de police de Casablanca, Tanger, Rabat, Agadir, Inzegane, Aït Melloul et Tikiouine. Selon un communiqué de la Direction générale, dix de ces nominations concernent des mouvements internes parmi les chefs de districts de police dans les villes d’Agadir, Aït Melloul, Tikiouine et Inzegane. Les autres désignations portent sur plusieurs fonctions relevant de différents services de la sûreté nationale. Elles comprennent notamment la nomination d’un chef de district de police à Casablanca, ainsi que la désignation de trois cadres de la police en uniforme à la tête d’équipes relevant des groupes chargés de la protection des installations sensibles à Rabat et Casablanca. La police cynotechnique est également concernée par cette nouvelle réorganisation, avec la nomination d’un responsable à la tête de la brigade spécialisée relevant de la zone de sûreté du port Tanger Med. À travers ces nominations, la DGSN affirme poursuivre sa stratégie de rotation dans les postes de responsabilité, afin de permettre à de nouvelles compétences policières d'accéder aux fonctions d’encadrement et de gestion. Cette démarche vise, selon l’institution, à améliorer le rendement des ressources humaines et à confier la gestion des services de police à des profils qualifiés, capables de mettre en œuvre les plans d’action destinés à renforcer la sécurité des citoyens et la protection de leurs biens. La Direction générale inscrit ces changements dans une dynamique continue de modernisation de ses structures et d’amélioration de l’efficacité des services de sécurité à l’échelle territoriale. items.title: Who will shape the new global order? Africa, India and the global south gather in Cape Town
items.description: As the old global order gives way to one not yet defined, the Thabo Mbeki Foundation and the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) will convene the fourth Cape Town Conversation on 23–24 November 2026 at The Westin. Themed Shaping Shared Futures in a Transforming World , the Conversation will bring together policymakers, business leaders, multilateral institutions, researchers and civil society from India, Africa, the wider Global South and the Global North. It will examine the partnerships and institutions the Global South needs to navigate and shape an emerging international order, and how shared priorities can be turned into action. “We meet at a moment when the old order is neither fully intact nor yet replaced. The Global South cannot be a bystander to what comes next. The Cape Town Conversation exists so that Africa, India and their partners can move from shared aspiration to shared action and shape the institutions and rules that will govern our common future,” said Max Boqwana, Chief Executive Officer of the Thabo Mbeki Foundation. A pivotal moment for Africa-India cooperation The reshaping of the global order brings new pressures, but also new possibilities for countries seeking greater agency over their development and partnerships. Across Africa, the call is for “Africa by Africans”, with priorities defined, financed and implemented on African terms. India, too, is pursuing strategic autonomy and nationally owned development. Bound by a long history of solidarity and nearly $100 billion in annual trade, the Africa-India partnership must now move towards co-creation and implementation. The convergence between Africa’s Agenda 2063 and India’s Viksit Bharat provides an important framework for this next phase. The Conversation was inaugurated in 2023, the year the African Union joined the G20, a moment that signalled optimism about a more representative global order. Since then, the landscape has shifted considerably. This edition will also explore how emerging technologies can widen the horizons of development rather than deepen existing divides. Six thematic tracks Through keynote addresses, panel discussions and focused expert engagements, the Conversation will move beyond conventional exchanges towards practical pathways for cooperation. Discussions are organised across six tracks: The New Age of Uncertainty: Power, Agency, and Sovereignty – Can African states convert collective weight into collective influence as multilateralism comes under strain? Commerce in an Age of Geopolitics: Trade, Markets, and Resilience – Can the Global South build markets and supply chains that reduce dependence and shape the rules of emerging industries? The New Compact for Development: Finance, Growth, and Capability – What should a new development pact look like as 2030 approaches? Claiming a Stake in Technology Futures: Innovation, Diffusion, and Access – Who will own and benefit from the AI economy? The New Geography of Growth: Connectivity, Corridors, and Logistics – Where should investment go, and how can infrastructure serve African production and regional integration? The Great Green Opportunity: Energy, Industry, and Economic Transformation – How can countries that supply the green transition’s minerals and energy also capture the manufacturing that follows? About the Cape Town Conversation The Cape Town Conversation is an annual South Africa-based platform, co-hosted by the Thabo Mbeki Foundation and the Observer Research Foundation, that brings together key stakeholders and new voices for a global conversation on contemporary issues of global governance. It is a leading international forum committed to amplifying the priorities and perspectives of the Global South.

items.title: Sam George challenges GMet to improve forecast accuracy and rebuild public confidence
items.description: Communications Minister Sam George has challenged the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) to improve the accuracy of its weather forecasts and rebuild public confidence in its services, acknowledging growing concerns about the agency’s performance. He says GMet must demonstrate measurable improvements in forecasting and ensure that critical weather information reaches communities in time to protect lives and property. Speaking at the agency’s maiden Annual General Meeting (AGM) and the inauguration of its new operational facility, Mr George said public concerns about the reliability of forecasts could not be dismissed. “Public confidence in GMet’s forecast must improve. Sections of the public are questioning the accuracy of forecasts and the reality of performance. We will not dismiss that perception and will not treat it lightly,” he said. He acknowledged that weather forecasting involves probabilities, changing atmospheric conditions and uncertainties but cautioned that these should not become excuses for poor communication or weak service delivery. The Minister said the devastating floods experienced in parts of the country in June 2026 had reinforced the need for more effective early warning systems. He stressed that forecasts and alerts must reach the right people at the right time to help them respond to potential dangers. “An early warning is only as good as its reach. Quality information is not enough. It must reach the right people at the right time, quickly and clearly,” he said. Mr George argued that publishing forecasts on GMet’s website and social media platforms was insufficient if the information failed to reach communities exposed to weather-related risks. He disclosed that the Ministry had directed the National Communications Authority (NCA) to work with GMet to operationalise the Common Alerting Protocol, which will allow official emergency warnings to be transmitted directly to citizens through Ghana’s telecommunications network. He said progress had been made since the June 29 floods in sending alerts and warnings about potential dangers across the country. The Minister urged the public to take the notifications seriously, assuring them that the alerts were genuine warnings issued by GMet. Mr George also announced progress towards new legislation intended to strengthen the agency’s institutional and operational capacity. He said the proposed legislation had received clearance from the Cabinet subcommittee and was expected to be presented to the full Cabinet at its next meeting. He expressed optimism that the bills could be laid before Parliament and passed early in 2027, following engagements with Parliament’s Select Committee. The proposed reforms are expected to transform GMet from an agency into an authority, with expanded powers and responsibilities. The Ministry, he said, would also support efforts to address technological gaps identified within the institution and strengthen its human resource capacity by filling existing vacancies. On staff welfare, Mr George disclosed that the government was working towards finalising issues relating to fair wages, salaries and conditions of service before the end of the first quarter of 2027. The Communications Minister cautioned GMet’s management against prioritising technological investments at the expense of the welfare and motivation of its workforce. He said the reliability of weather forecasts and prediction models depended not only on sophisticated systems but also on the personnel responsible for collecting and analysing data. “You can have the best systems, but if you have a demoralized workforce, those systems are not going to be efficient. They are going to be expensive ornaments in your building,” he warned. He maintained that even ordinary equipment could deliver better results when operated by a motivated workforce. Mr George also urged management to make opportunities for international conferences and training programmes accessible to more employees rather than concentrating them among a few senior officials. He said broader access to such opportunities would help develop the expertise of other staff members and prepare them for future leadership roles. The Minister said the increasing frequency, intensity and cost of weather-related hazards had made early warning systems, emergency preparedness and climate resilience central to the government’s development agenda. Referencing the June 2026 floods, he said Ghana could no longer afford to wait for disasters before taking preventive action. He cited President John Dramani Mahama’s observation that climate change was significantly increasing the volume of rainfall received annually, underscoring the need for reliable scientific information, effective communication and coordinated emergency responses. Mr George disclosed that following the floods, the President directed the establishment of specialised committees, including an early warning committee and an emergency communications committee, with GMet represented on both. The committees are expected to strengthen coordination among government institutions, technical agencies and security services to ensure timely and consistent information reaches the public. He also highlighted ongoing partnerships with international institutions, including the World Meteorological Organization and the Kingdom of Denmark, to strengthen technical cooperation and modernise Ghana’s meteorological services. According to him, the Ghana-Denmark Strategic Sector Cooperation Programme has supported a review of GMet’s information technology and digitalisation gaps, with a roadmap developed to address the identified challenges. Mr George urged the agency to use its newly launched 2027–2031 Strategic Plan to deliver measurable improvements in forecasting, public communication and national preparedness. He said the success of the reforms would ultimately be measured by the reliability of forecasts, the reach of early warnings and the extent to which lives and property were protected.

items.title: Nigerian woman found dead in Canada days after returning from work
items.description: A 26 year old Nigerian woman, Ayotomiwa Chelsea Omotosho, has been found dead in Canada, days after returning home from work, leaving her family and members of the Nigerian community seeking answers about the circumstances surrounding her death. Chelsea, a graduate of Humber College, was reportedly found lifeless on Thursday, November 19, 2026, after returning from work the previous day. According to a fundraising appeal launched by friends and members of the Nigerian community in Canada, the cause of her death remains unknown. “On Wednesday, November 18, 2026, Chelsea returned home from work, just as she had on countless other days. Tragically, on Thursday, November 19, she was found lifeless. At this time, the cause of her death remains unknown,” the appeal stated. Chelsea moved from Nigeria to Canada in May 2024 to study Media Management at Humber College. She graduated in November 2025 and later secured employment in the healthcare sector at The Residence on Yonge. She was also an active member of the MOLC Choir, where she became known within the Nigerian community in Canada. Friends described her as a warm and dedicated young woman, saying her sudden death had left those who knew her devastated. The youngest of four children, Chelsea is survived by her parents and siblings in Nigeria, who are now mourning her loss from thousands of kilometres away. Her family, alongside members of the Nigerian community in Canada, is making arrangements for a memorial service and burial in the country. The fundraising appeal said her loved ones were still seeking answers about what led to her death as they prepare to lay her to rest.
