items.title: Minority asks government to enforce Ghanaian-only retail trade restrictions after Suame clashes
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has condemned the violence and forced closures reported at Suame Magazine on November 23, while demanding that the government urgently enforce the law reserving certain categories of retail trade for Ghanaians. The caucus said the frustration among Ghanaian traders was justified, accusing the government of failing to protect their livelihoods despite repeated calls for action and a commitment to establish an enforcement task force. In a statement signed by the Ranking Member of Parliament’s Trade, Industry and Tourism Committee, Michael Okyere Baafi, the Minority said Ghanaian traders had petitioned, protested and waited for more than a decade for the law to be enforced. It noted that Parliament, in July 2026, again reserved market trading, petty trading and hawking for Ghanaians under the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Act. The government subsequently promised on August 18 to establish an inter-agency task force to enforce the law. However, the Minority said three months after the commitment, traders had seen little change. “They have kept faith with the law. The State has not kept faith with them,” the statement said. The caucus, however, stressed that its support for the traders did not amount to an endorsement of the violence reported at Suame Magazine. “The Minority cannot, however, condone the assaults and forced closures of 23 November. Violence harms the traders’ own cause and puts Ghanaians at risk,” it said. It argued that the failure of the state to enforce the law had contributed to the growing tensions, insisting that the responsibility for enforcement rested with government agencies. The Minority also identified gaps in the legislation, particularly the absence of clear definitions for terms such as “petty trading” and “stall”. It said the Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry had the power to address the ambiguity through a legislative instrument but had failed to do so. “Ghanaian and foreign traders alike are left unsure where the line falls, and that uncertainty is what breeds confrontation,” the statement said. The caucus further criticised successive governments for responding to disputes over retail trading with task forces whose enforcement efforts eventually lapse. It said Ghana needed a lasting solution rather than another temporary intervention. The Minority has therefore called on the government to ensure sustained enforcement of the retail trade restrictions by state agencies, beginning at Suame Magazine, Abossey Okai and Kwame Nkrumah Circle. It also wants the government to urgently lay before Parliament a legislative instrument defining the activities reserved for Ghanaians and to enforce the law against landlords who unlawfully rent out stalls and individuals who act as fronts for foreign traders. On concerns about unfair competition, the caucus has called for investigations into complaints by Ghanaian traders over under-pricing and counterfeit spare parts, urging Customs and the Ghana Standards Authority to publish their findings. It further wants the government to support local spare-parts dealers with access to trade credit and pooled importing arrangements to help them compete on price. Other demands include the publication of an account of the task force’s work since August, investigations into the November 23 incidents and guarantees for the safety of all traders. The Minority has also asked the government to explain how the restrictions on retail trading are being reconciled with Ghana’s obligations under the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) framework and to engage Nigeria to prevent tensions from escalating. “The Ghanaian trader has done everything the law asks and has been let down. We do not ask traders to be patient any longer. We ask Government to do its job,” the statement said. Mr Okyere Baafi said the Minority would file an urgent question for the Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry to answer the concerns raised. The caucus added that Ghana’s position as host of the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) meant the country’s handling of the dispute would be watched across the continent.

items.title: Le Sénégal lance la formulation de sa Stratégie nationale de transition agro-écologique
items.description: Le ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Souveraineté alimentaire et de l’Élevage, Cheikh Oumar Ba, et son collègue de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique, Dr Aliou Gori Diouf, ont coprésidé, mardi 24 novembre, la première réunion du comité de pilotage (Copil) de la Stratégie nationale de transition agro-écologique du Sénégal (Sntaes). Face aux urgences climatiques et à la dégradation des sols, le Sénégal réinvente ses systèmes alimentaires. RUFISQUE – Offrant un cadre national unifié, lisible et opérationnel, la Stratégie nationale de transition agro-écologique du Sénégal (Snaes) pousse le gouvernement à unir ses forces pour dépasser les cloisonnements administratifs et lier l’avenir agricole aux écosystèmes. En présence d’une diversité d’acteurs, les deux ministres sectoriels ont pris part, hier, mardi 24 novembre, à la première réunion du Copil. Le ministre de l’Environnement et de la Transition écologique, Dr Aliou Gori Diouf, a insisté sur les liens indissociables entre l’agriculture et les écosystèmes. Dans ce sens, au lieu de privilégier la notion de développement durable, il met l’accent sur celle de « soutenabilité ». Son collègue en charge de l’Agriculture, de la Souveraineté alimentaire et de l’Élevage, Cheikh Oumar Ba, est en phase avec cette approche. Selon lui, la souveraineté alimentaire ne se mesure pas uniquement au volume produit. « Elle exige avant tout de préserver et de régénérer nos ressources naturelles, d’augmenter la résilience de nos exploitations familiales et de garantir à chaque citoyenne et à chaque citoyen un accès régulier à une alimentation saine et abordable », a-t-il déclaré. Pour lui, l’agroécologie permet de changer de paradigme face aux défis et aux vulnérabilités. « L’agroécologie est bien plus qu’une option marginale ou un ajustement technique », mais une véritable démarche de transformation de nos systèmes agricoles et alimentaires, alliant « la rigueur de la recherche scientifique au savoir paysan, et l’innovation technologique à l’action collective », estime le ministre. Le ministère de l’Agriculture attend de ce processus, à la fois articulé aux instruments climatiques et ancré dans les territoires, qu’il réponde à trois exigences : un diagnostic partagé, un cadre de coordination efficace et un plan d’action chiffré. Pour Jean Michel Wally Sène, de la Dynamique pour une transition agro-écologique au Sénégal (DyTaes), cette Sntaes est un instrument de coordination intersectorielle autour de l’agroécologie et n’exclut pas les autres ministères. Il souhaite un co-pilotage effectif pour faire avancer l’agroécologie. Mohamed DIÈNE (Correspondant)

items.title: Sudan loses OPCW council seat amid chemical weapons allegations
items.description: Sudan has lost its seat on the Executive Council of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), amid mounting international pressure over allegations that chemical weapons were used during the country’s ongoing war. The decision came yesterday during the organisation’s 31st Conference of the States Parties in The Hague, Netherlands, where Morocco, Angola, Cameroon, Tanzania and Tunisia were elected on Tuesday to represent Africa on the 41-member council from 2027. ‘Sudan investigation under scrutiny’ Addressing the conference, OPCW Director-General Sabrina Dallafior said Sudan’s case remained before the Executive Council and urged countries with relevant evidence to share it, even confidentially. “It is disappointing that despite concerns being raised in the OPCW and media reporting of the allegations, so far, no detailed information has been shared with the Secretariat,” she said in her opening statement . Dallafior said she had met Sudanese representatives and offered technical assistance for their national investigation, adding that she hoped its findings would be circulated to member states. ‘Britain demands credible investigation’ Britain renewed its call for Sudan to investigate the allegations, warning that reports suggested increasingly systematic chemical weapons use. “If substantiated, such use would pose a grave threat not only to the people of Sudan but to the wider region,” the UK statement to the conference on 24 November said . London called on Sudan to complete a “thorough, transparent, impartial and credible national investigation ” and share its findings with the OPCW in full. In April 2025, the United States concluded that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) had used chemical weapons in violation of international law and imposed sanctions on Sudan. Washington increased pressure in March 2026, threatening to reconsider Sudan’s position on the Executive Council unless the allegations were urgently addressed. In September 2026, investigations published by The New York Times and T he Washington Post revealed further details about Sudan’s alleged production and use of chemical weapons, building on France 24’s initial reporting last year. Share article The post Sudan loses OPCW council seat amid chemical weapons allegations appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Le Réseau Migration Développement (REMIDEV) réclame une enquête impartiale sur le drame de Lompoul
items.description: Face à la multiplication des drames liés à l’émigration irrégulière, le Réseau Migration Développement (REMIDEV) appelle à un changement de paradigme dans la gouvernance migratoire au Sénégal. Dans un communiqué rendu public le 24 novembre 2026, l’organisation et ses membres dénoncent les atteintes aux droits humains, réclament une enquête impartiale sur le naufrage de Lompoul et invitent les autorités à privilégier des politiques migratoires respectueuses des droits et des aspirations des jeunes. Le drame de Lompoul continue de susciter des réactions. Après la mort de dizaines de jeunes candidats à l’émigration, le Réseau Migration Développement (REMIDEV) monte au créneau. Dans un communiqué publié le 24 novembre, l’organisation revient sur les circonstances du naufrage survenu le 6 novembre 2026 au large du village de Lompoul et interpelle les autorités sénégalaises sur la gestion des flux migratoires. Selon les éléments rapportés dans le document, 44 jeunes garçons et filles ont perdu la vie dans ce drame. Environ 150 personnes se trouvaient à bord de la pirogue, d’après l’unique rescapé. Le chavirement serait intervenu alors que l’embarcation approchait des côtes de Lompoul, après l’apparition d’une patrouille de la Marine nationale. La peur d’une arrestation aurait poussé plusieurs passagers à se jeter à l’eau pour rejoindre la plage à la nage. La forte houle, la surcharge de la pirogue et des avaries matérielles auraient également contribué au naufrage. Pour le REMIDEV, les circonstances exactes de cette tragédie doivent être établies. L’organisation souligne que les autorités sénégalaises n’ont pas encore publié de rapport d’enquête permettant de faire la lumière sur le déroulement de l’intervention des forces de défense et de sécurité en mer. Elle exige ainsi « l’ouverture d’une enquête impartiale afin d’établir les responsabilités dans la survenue du drame de Lompoul ». Cette nouvelle tragédie intervient dans un contexte marqué par une recrudescence des tentatives de départ vers l’Europe. Le réseau rappelle que, le 10 novembre, la Marine nationale avait annoncé avoir secouru 759 migrants répartis dans quatre pirogues en une seule journée. Il évoque également les arrivées de migrants aux îles Canaries ainsi que plusieurs autres incidents signalés dans la presse sénégalaise le 23 novembre, notamment le chavirement d’une pirogue au large de Yenne, la disparition d’une embarcation partie de Yoff avec 175 jeunes à son bord et l’interception de candidats à l’émigration à Fimela et en Gambie. Un malaise économique et social profond Au-delà des opérations de surveillance et d’interception, le REMIDEV invite à s’interroger sur les causes profondes de cette détermination des jeunes à risquer leur vie en mer. L’organisation pointe notamment une conjoncture économique et sociale morose, caractérisée par la hausse du chômage, la baisse des investissements et des financements ainsi que l’absence de politiques efficaces d’emploi et d’insertion professionnelle. Le secteur de la pêche figure également parmi les préoccupations soulevées. Le réseau évoque une crise qui pousse de nombreux jeunes pêcheurs à rechercher d’autres sources de revenus, certains étant amenés à participer à l’organisation de la migration dite irrégulière. Il met notamment en cause la raréfaction des ressources halieutiques et des accords de pêche qu’il juge « léonins ». À ces difficultés s’ajoutent, selon le REMIDEV, un climat politique ayant érodé la confiance des jeunes, le durcissement des procédures d’octroi de visas par les représentations diplomatiques étrangères ainsi qu'un manque de coordination des politiques migratoires entre le Sénégal et ses pays voisins. Face à ce tableau, l’organisation estime que les réponses essentiellement sécuritaires ne sauraient constituer une solution durable. « La lutte contre les réseaux de migration irrégulière, aussi légitime soit-elle, ne saurait justifier des atteintes systématiques aux droits humains fondamentaux », martèle-t-elle. Le réseau dénonce également le traitement réservé aux migrants sur le continent africain, jugeant « inadmissible que des Africains soient pourchassés, brutalisés et humiliés sur le sol africain au nom de mesures de sécurité inspirées par l’Union européenne ». Pour une nouvelle gouvernance migratoire Dans ses recommandations, le REMIDEV appelle à un changement de paradigme dans la gouvernance migratoire. Il demande notamment aux autorités sénégalaises d'adopter une politique migratoire nationale assortie de programmes respectueux des droits fondamentaux et des aspirations des citoyens. L’organisation invite également les autorités consulaires et diplomatiques étrangères à assouplir les procédures d’octroi de visas, dont le durcissement contribuerait, selon elle, au développement de la migration irrégulière. Par ailleurs, elle réclame la mise en place d’un cadre permanent de dialogue entre la société civile et les autorités afin de favoriser une meilleure gouvernance des politiques migratoires. Le réseau rappelle, dans la même dynamique, les engagements pris par l’État en matière de réduction du chômage et du coût de la vie, d’amélioration de l’accès aux financements, d’industrialisation et de gestion des ressources publiques. En associant ses membres aux condoléances adressées aux familles endeuillées, le REMIDEV insiste sur la nécessité de dépasser la seule logique répressive. Pour l'organisation, la réponse à la crise migratoire passe aussi par des perspectives économiques et sociales capables de redonner aux jeunes des raisons de construire leur avenir au Sénégal. A.N

items.title: Tinubu’s govt has made everyone poor — Obi
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening poverty in the country, saying Nigerians should not continue to endure the hardship. Obi said his proposed government with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso would prioritise job creation, production, poverty reduction and the responsible management of public resources. He spoke on Wednesday at the NDC town hall meeting in Edo State, where he urged Nigerians to support the party in the 2027 general election. “Tinubu has put everybody into poverty; that poverty must not continue,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor said his ambition was to move Nigeria away from a consumption-driven economy towards one focused on production, arguing that such a shift would create jobs and improve living conditions. “We want to build a new Nigeria that is possible. We want to remove Nigeria from consumption to production so all of you can have jobs. We want to pull Nigerians out of poverty, we want to build a country that cares for everybody,” he said. Obi also promised to tackle corruption and ensure that public resources were deployed for the benefit of citizens. “We want to build a country, where people will no longer steal public money. Public money must be used for public good. That’s what we want to do,” he said. Calling on supporters to remain vigilant during the 2027 elections, the NDC candidate urged voters to stay at their polling units after casting their ballots until the votes were counted. He said the party would not want its votes compromised through electoral malpractice. “We want you to go out in 2027, you’re our polling agents. When you vote, don’t go home. Stay there until your vote is counted. We don’t want them to rig us out. We must get it right this time because we want to build a better society,” Obi said. He urged Nigerians to vote for him and Kwankwaso, saying their proposed administration would be led by people committed to serving the country. “Vote Kwankwaso and I to start that new Nigeria. We want to make sure that we have a government of people, who have compassion, who have commitment, who have the energy to do the job,” he added. Obi further pledged to build a society where opportunities would not depend on personal connections or family background. “We want to build a society where a child of nobody can be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. items.title: Autonomisation des femmes : 135 femmes de Kédougou formées à la transformation des céréales
items.description: Cent trente-cinq femmes de Kédougou, Saraya et Salémata ont bénéficié, les 24 et 25 novembre, d’une formation aux techniques de transformation des céréales locales et à l’utilisation de moulins modernes, dans le cadre du Programme d’éducation et d’autonomisation des femmes de la Première Dame, Marie Khone Faye. Durant deux jours, les participantes ont été formées à la transformation du fonio, du mil, du maïs et du sorgho, ainsi qu’aux normes d’hygiène, de conservation, de conditionnement et de commercialisation. Elles ont également été initiées au fonctionnement et à l’entretien des moulins qui leur seront remis. Selon Bassirou Ngom, responsable de l’autonomisation des femmes au sein du programme, ces équipements de dernière génération disposent d’un système hybride combinant énergie électrique et thermique, avec une possibilité d’alimentation solaire. Une innovation destinée à faciliter leur utilisation, notamment dans les zones confrontées aux difficultés d’accès à l’électricité. Présidente de la section féminine de l’Association des personnes handicapées de Kédougou, Kadioatiou Dia a salué cette initiative, notamment la prise en compte des femmes vivant avec un handicap. Elle a exprimé sa gratitude à la Première Dame et promis que les bénéficiaires feraient bon usage des équipements pour développer leurs activités. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: Bandits abduct six in midnight raid on Kaduna community
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Suspected bandits have abducted six residents during a midnight attack on Mama G area, near MPH, Millennium City, in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The attackers reportedly stormed two houses around 11:30pm on Tuesday, shooting sporadically and initially abducting nine persons. However, three of the victims, including an elderly woman, a mother and her toddler, were later released, leaving six others in the custody of the abductors. The incident has heightened fears among residents of Millennium City, who say repeated attacks have made life increasingly difficult, forcing some homeowners and tenants to abandon their houses over fears of kidnapping. One of the residents, whose wife was among those abducted, was seen weeping as he appealed for help to secure her release. He expressed concern about her health, saying she had difficulty walking before the incident. “I don’t know her condition as we speak because she is having problems walking, and now they have taken her away. I’m appealing to whoever can help me rescue her from them,” he said. Another resident, Hassan Salihu, said residents heard gunshots around 11:30pm on Tuesday and immediately contacted one another to establish where the shooting was taking place. “When we heard gunshots, we started communicating with other residents to know the exact location. We later discovered it was here in our community. “We alerted the soldiers, and they came through Keke A and remained here until 4am, but we didn’t see the abductors leaving the area,” he said. Salihu appealed to the Kaduna State Government and security authorities to establish a military outpost in the community, particularly along routes allegedly used by the attackers. Similarly, Adamu Muhammad Maina said the attack threw residents into confusion, adding that nine people were initially taken from two neighbouring houses. “It was a terrible situation. Nine people were initially abducted from our neighbours’ houses. Four people were abducted from one house, including a woman and her toddler, but they were released,” he said. He explained that five other residents were taken from the second house, including an elderly woman who was subsequently released because of her inability to walk. “Now we have six people with the bandits, and nobody knows their location,” he added. A female resident, who pleaded anonymity, said the persistent attacks had traumatised the community, forcing some landlords and tenants to abandon their homes. “We are traumatised because most house owners are now abandoning their houses. We find it difficult to sleep inside our homes, so we are pleading with the relevant agencies, including the state and Federal Governments, to come to our aid,” she said. Residents also disclosed that suspected bandits had attempted to invade the community on Monday night but were repelled by security operatives before returning on Tuesday night. When contacted, the Kaduna State Police Command Public Relations Officer, DSP Mansir Hassan, said he would respond after obtaining full details of the incident. The post Bandits abduct six in midnight raid on Kaduna community appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Una víctima de violencia machista, en un acto del Ayuntamiento de Madrid: “Vuestras políticas no me representan y menos aún vuestros aliados”
items.description: Laura ha contado durante 20 minutos cómo su expareja la maltrató durante el tiempo que duró su relación. Lo ha hecho despacio, ante una sala llena de periodistas y autoridades. Todos en silencio. Ha hablado de cómo al principio era bonito, un romance al uso, y después llegaron los celos, el control, las recriminaciones constantes, las vejaciones, los desprecios, la violencia física. Lo ha hecho este miércoles en un acto del Ayuntamiento de Madrid por el 25N , el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer, en el que ha participado invitada por el consistorio. Justo antes de terminar, con los ojos fijos en la fila de butacas donde se sentaban el alcalde, José Luis Martínez-Almeida (PP), y otros miembros de su equipo de gobierno, ha dicho: “He pensado mucho si venir aquí hoy o no, porque siendo mujer, vuestras políticas no me representan y menos aún vuestros aliados en el poder”. Con esto último se refiere a Vox y los pactos de gobierno ― los que ya existen en otras administraciones y los futuros ― entre ambos partidos. Sus palabras han resonado entre los presentes un día después de que la portavoz de la formación de ultraderecha en la capital defendiera, convencida y de forma tajante, lo siguiente: “La violencia de género, esa que cuelga de la ideología de género, por supuesto que la niego. Tal cual. La niego. Por supuesto”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Police arrest six over investment fraud, romance scam, sextortion
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force has arrested six suspects over alleged involvement in investment fraud, romance scams, sextortion, cyberstalking, money laundering and other cyber-related offences. The arrests followed separate intelligence-led investigations by operatives of the Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre (NPF-NCCC), including a probe into an investment scam involving ₦40 million and a transnational romance fraud network targeting elderly Canadians. The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of the NPF-NCCC, Akaniyene Ezima, disclosed this on Wednesday, detailing the investigations and financial transactions allegedly linked to the suspects. ₦684m traced to investment fraud network Ezima said the investment fraud investigation followed a petition by a couple who alleged that they were defrauded of ₦40 million between February 16 and 21, 2025, through a fraudulent online employment and investment scheme. According to him, the victims were initially contacted through unsolicited text messages advertising an allegedly lucrative remote employment opportunity operating under the name AliExpress Shopverse. He said the victims were offered ₦400 for completing simple online tasks, including liking merchants’ pages, before being introduced to a higher-value investment arrangement disguised as merchant trade optimisation. The victims were reportedly assured that their investments would be refunded alongside guaranteed commissions. “Acting on these fraudulent representations, the victims made successful transfers amounting to ₦40,000,000.00. Upon receipt of the funds, the fraudsters severed communication with the victims and diverted the funds through a network of personal, corporate and intermediary bank accounts,” he said. Ezima said digital forensic analysis and financial intelligence investigations led to the identification of Christian Chukwuemeka Ahaji as the principal recipient and controller of accounts operating under the business name SP-Emmy Tradelinks. Further investigations reportedly established that the business name was unregistered and that several accounts linked to it were used to receive and redistribute funds. He said a forensic audit identified 42 bank accounts connected to the investigation, comprising 26 personal accounts belonging to Ahaji, 12 business accounts associated with SP-Emmy Tradelinks and four intermediary accounts. According to him, the 26 personal accounts recorded cumulative inflows of ₦217.3 million, while the 12 business accounts recorded ₦334.8 million. The four intermediary accounts, allegedly operated by Jude Chukwuka Oneh, Safiyya Aliyu, Salamatu Adamu and Sadiya Yusuf Zubairu, recorded inflows of ₦132 million. The combined inflows across the 42 accounts amounted to ₦684,161,496, the police said. Ezima disclosed that transaction analysis also established financial links between Oneh and Ahaji, with Oneh allegedly transferring ₦26.67 million through 58 transactions into accounts associated with SP-Emmy Tradelinks and another ₦3.15 million through eight transactions into Ahaji’s personal accounts. He added that further analysis identified disbursements through Point-of-Sale channels and payments linked to high-value assets, property improvements, vehicle purchases and online betting platforms. The police said investigations were continuing to establish the relationship between the transactions and the alleged proceeds of crime, as well as trace and recover any assets acquired through unlawful activities. Three arrested over Canada romance scam In another operation, the NPF-NCCC, working with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP), arrested three additional suspects in connection with an alleged transnational romance fraud network targeting elderly residents of Canada between 2020 and 2024. The suspects were identified as Emmanuel Imoni, 34; Nathaniel Imoni, 39; and Akpofagha Abodei. Ezima said the network allegedly used fictitious identities on social media and other digital communication platforms to establish deceptive romantic relationships with victims before persuading them to transfer money under fraudulent pretences. The proceeds were allegedly moved through financial intermediaries and cryptocurrency platforms across Canada, the United States, Nigeria, Turkey and Kenya. He said the latest arrests followed earlier arrests of some suspects on October 23, 2026, and subsequent investigations involving cryptocurrency tracing, financial intelligence analysis and beneficiary profiling. According to him, Emmanuel Imoni was identified as the primary beneficiary of funds converted from cryptocurrency, particularly Tether (USDT), into naira by an earlier arrested suspect, Uka Chidiebere Gerald. Investigators also allegedly discovered that bank accounts belonging to Imoni’s wife, Abodei, and his brother, Nathaniel, were used to receive additional funds when transactions exceeded the limits applicable to his personal accounts. The police said financial analysis of the accounts revealed transactions valued at CA$573,040 for Emmanuel Imoni, CA$58,258 for Nathaniel Imoni and CA$299,528 for Abodei. The combined value of the transactions was approximately CA$930,826. Ezima said asset-tracing investigations also led operatives to identify two three-bedroom residential apartments in Wuye, Abuja, allegedly acquired by Emmanuel Imoni with proceeds of the fraudulent activities. Items recovered during the operation included nine mobile phones, an Apple laptop, an Apple Watch, SIM cards, a flash drive, a Toyota Camry and a Toyota RAV4. He said the recovered digital devices were undergoing forensic examination to establish the extent of the alleged offences, identify additional financial connections and determine whether other persons were involved. The AIG said investigations were continuing in collaboration with the RCMP to identify additional suspects and trace and recover proceeds of the alleged crimes. Police arrest suspect over sextortion, cyberstalking In a separate case, the Police arrested John Ifeanyi Nwankwo over allegations of sextortion, cyberstalking and the non-consensual distribution of intimate images and videos of a former partner. Ezima said the investigation followed a petition dated June 16, 2026, in which the complainant alleged that she was threatened, secretly recorded and exposed to the circulation of intimate materials following the breakdown of her relationship with the suspect. According to him, the complainant began the relationship with Nwankwo in February 2026 and had noticed a closed-circuit television (CCTV) camera installed in a bathroom at his residence. He said when she questioned the suspect about the surveillance equipment, she was assured that it was not functional. However, following a financial disagreement and the subsequent termination of the relationship, the suspect allegedly threatened the complainant and circulated her intimate pictures and video recordings to her friends, associates and employer without her consent. Ezima said operatives obtained arrest and search warrants from a court of competent jurisdiction before arresting Nwankwo on November 4, 2026. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly admitted installing surveillance cameras in his residence and deliberately recording intimate moments involving the complainant without her knowledge or consent. The police spokesperson said investigations further revealed that the recordings were transferred to the suspect’s mobile phone and circulated through WhatsApp to individuals within the complainant’s personal and professional circles. The suspect reportedly attributed his actions to retaliation following disagreements in the relationship. Items recovered included a CCTV storage hard drive containing the intimate recordings, an MTN internet router and an iPhone 14 Pro Max. Ezima said the items had been registered as exhibits for further investigation. He warned against the misuse of digital surveillance technology and communication platforms to violate privacy, facilitate harassment and cause reputational and psychological harm. The Police said investigations into the cases remained ongoing. The post Police arrest six over investment fraud, romance scam, sextortion appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Investissement en Algérie : l’AAPI « libère » 100 hectares dans 13 wilayas
items.description: Dans le but de répondre aux requêtes des investisseurs toujours en quête d'assiettes foncières, l'Agence algérienne de promotion de l’investissement (AAPI) passe à l'action. L'agence dirigée par Omar Rekkache vient en effet d'annoncer la « libération » d’un important lot d'assiettes foncières destinées à abriter des investissements . Une décision qui vient renforcer les possibilités d’implantation de projets dans plusieurs régions du pays. Investissement en Algérie : 100 hectares répartis sur 13 wilayas En effet, le Conseil d’administration de l’Agence algérienne de promotion de l’investissement (AAPI) a approuvé, mardi 24 novembre 2026, lors de sa troisième session ordinaire, la mise à disposition de 100 nouvelles assiettes foncières destinées à être publiées prochainement sur la plateforme numérique de l’investisseur. Présidée par le président du Conseil, Abderrazak Azab, en présence du directeur général de l’Agence, Omar Rekkache, cette réunion s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’application des dispositions réglementaires encadrant l’organisation de l’AAPI ainsi que les conditions et modalités d’attribution du foncier économique destiné à la réalisation de projets d’investissement. Au total, ces nouvelles assiettes représentent une superficie globale de 100,29 hectares. Elles sont réparties entre 13 wilayas : Constantine, El Meghaïer, Khenchela, Béchar, Mostaganem, Batna, El Bayadh, Boumerdès, Oran, Annaba, Bouira, Jijel et Béni Abbès. Leur publication sur la plateforme numérique de l’investisseur permettra ainsi aux opérateurs économiques de prendre connaissance des nouvelles opportunités foncières proposées dans ces territoires. Dix projets d’investissement retenus Par ailleurs, les travaux de cette session ont également porté sur l’examen des dossiers de projets d’investissement candidats à l’obtention d’assiettes foncières déjà publiées sur la plateforme numérique. À l’issue de l’étude des demandes présentées par les investisseurs concernés, l’AAPI a donné son approbation à dix projets d’investissement pour bénéficier du foncier économique. Une gouvernance interministérielle À noter que le Conseil d’administration de l’AAPI regroupe les secrétaires généraux des secteurs ministériels concernés par la politique d’investissement et la gestion du foncier économique en Algérie. Il comprend notamment les représentants des ministères des Affaires étrangères, des Hydrocarbures, des Mines, des Finances, de l’Industrie, de l’Agriculture, de l’Énergie, des Collectivités locales, de l’Urbanisme, du Commerce extérieur et intérieur, des Ressources en eau, du Tourisme, de l’Environnement et de l’Emploi. L’article Investissement en Algérie : l'AAPI « libère » 100 hectares dans 13 wilayas est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: French Ambassador commends Ato Forson’s management of Ghana’s economy
items.description: France’s Ambassador to Ghana, Diarra Dimé-Labille, has expressed confidence in the government’s management of the economy, commending Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson for what she describes as impressive performance. Speaking during a courtesy visit to the Finance Minister on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, the Ambassador said France was encouraged by Ghana’s economic performance. “We are all quite impressed with how you are doing well when it comes to the economy,” she said. Diarra Dimé-Labille, who was appointed France’s Ambassador to Ghana by the President of the French Republic in September 2025, reaffirmed the country’s interest in Ghana’s economic progress. Dr Ato Forson, in response, expressed Ghana’s appreciation for France’s longstanding partnership and support, particularly in strengthening the capabilities of the Ghana Armed Forces. He said France had played a role in facilitating Ghana’s access to military equipment and aircraft through connections established by the Ambassador’s predecessor. The Finance Minister acknowledged the contribution of the French government, expressing gratitude for the support extended to Ghana. “We are extremely grateful to you and your government,” he said.

items.title: Industrie de défense et de sécurité : le Roi préside la cérémonie de signature de deux conventions-cadres
items.description: Le Roi Mohammed VI, accompagné du Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan, a présidé, ce mercredi 25 novembre 2026 au Palais Royal de Rabat, la cérémonie de signature de deux conventions-cadres portant sur le financement de la feuille de route pour le développement de l’industrie de défense et de sécurité et la mobilisation du secteur privé et financier national pour son déploiement. Au début de cette cérémonie, Ali Seddiki, Directeur Général de l’Agence Marocaine de Développement des Investissements et des Exportations (AMDIE), que le Roi a bien voulu charger de veiller à l’élaboration opérationnelle de la mise en œuvre de cette feuille de route, a prononcé une allocution devant le Souverain dans laquelle il a notamment souligné que sous l’Egide du Roi, le Maroc a été transformé et est aujourd’hui un leader industriel continental, fier de son présent et confiant dans son avenir, précisant que le Royaume, guidé par la Vision Royale, s’est imposé parmi les nations à émerger dans des secteurs de pointe. Rappelant que le Souverain a, à l’occasion de la séance de travail du 18 novembre dernier, donné Ses Hautes Instructions pour accélérer le déploiement de la feuille de route de l’ »Offre Maroc » pour le développement de l’industrie nationale de défense et de sécurité, il a soutenu que celle-ci s’inscrit résolument dans la continuité des Réalisations Royales pour un Maroc industriel, émergent, fort de ses potentialités, de ses atouts et de son capital humain. « La Vision Royale est à présent de bâtir une Base Industrielle et Technologique de Défense et de Sécurité nationale souveraine, performante, innovante et compétitive », a-t-il assuré, notant que ce secteur incarnera l’Ambition Royale en faveur de l’économie nationale, une économie à l’heure des grandes transformations, projetée vers l’avenir, et où les fonds d’investissement et les marchés de capitaux occuperont une grande place et permettront à l’audace entrepreneuriale de prospérer. Seddiki a ainsi indiqué qu’en février 2022, l’objectif de porter la part de l’investissement privé à deux tiers de l’investissement national en 2035 a été présenté à Sa Majesté le Roi, précisant que c’est dans cette haute orientation que devra s’inscrire la nouvelle industrie de défense et de sécurité. Il a, en outre, noté que le Souverain a appelé dans le discours du Trône de juillet dernier à élargir qualitativement l’accès au financement bancaire et non bancaire afin de soutenir en priorité les PME, l’innovation, l’industrialisation et l’exportation. Grâce à la vision éclairée du Roi, le secteur des industries de défense et de sécurité à vocation internationale offre une opportunité d’investissement historique aux opérateurs privés dans des métiers nouveaux et innovants, a-t-il affirmé. Il a, dans ce cadre, souligné que sous l’Impulsion du Suverain, un élan de mobilisation sans précédent des partenaires publics a permis de réunir une enveloppe de près de 22 milliards de dirhams autour de ce chantier stratégique, précisant que l’application des hautes orientations royales permettra aux industriels installés au Maroc de couvrir 40% des besoins des Forces Armées Royales et des organes de sécurité. Il a, par ailleurs, fait savoir qu’à terme, cette industrie devra générer au moins 50 milliards de dirhams par an de revenus dont plus de 65% à l’export, indiquant que cet élan collectif permettra à l‘industrie de défense et de sécurité nationale de créer au moins 50.000 emplois directs et indirects à l’horizon 2035. Fidèle aux hautes directives royales, une place centrale a été accordée au capital humain, notamment par la formation, a-t-il dit, expliquant qu’un écosystème national de recherche et de développement sera mis en place et mobilisera compétences locales et Marocains du monde au service de cette ambition. Et en concrétisation de ces instructions pour une mise en œuvre rapide et effective de la feuille de route et de ses organes de gouvernance, l’Agence Stratégique, au cœur du dispositif, suivra l’ensemble des engagements des acteurs publics et privés concernés. Dans ce cadre, le Roi a bien voulu baptiser la future Agence Stratégique du nom « DIFAA- Defense Industry Facilitation and Acceleration Agency » (L’Agence Marocaine de l’Industrie de Défense et de Sécurité). L’Agence DIFAA permettra de développer la production d’armement, notamment les drones et systèmes autonomes, les systèmes terrestres, les systèmes navals, l'électronique de défense et la cyberdéfense, ainsi que l’intelligence artificielle. Elle mettra en œuvre la stratégie de l’État en matière de développement du secteur, à travers la promotion de l’investissement, la gestion des dispositifs d’appui et la structuration de la base industrielle nationale. Elle mobilisera les leviers de la compensation industrielle, de la commande publique, du foncier, des compétences et de l’innovation au service de la souveraineté industrielle du Royaume et du rayonnement international de l’offre nationale. A cette occasion, le Roi a présidé la cérémonie de signature des deux conventions-cadres. La première convention-cadre, relative au financement de la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route pour le développement de l’industrie nationale de défense et de sécurité, a été signée par le ministre de l’Intérieur, Abdelouafi Laftit, le ministre de l’Economie, des Finances et de la Performance publique, Fouzi Lekjaa, le ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce, de l’Investissement et de l’Inclusion économique, Ryad Mezzour, le ministre délégué auprès de la Cheffe du gouvernement, chargé de l’Administration de la Défense Nationale, Abdeltif Loudyi, le Directeur général de l’AMDIE, Ali Seddiki, le Directeur général de la Caisse de Dépôt et de Gestion (CDG), Khalid Safir, la Présidente du directoire du Fonds Hassan II pour le développement économique et social, Dounia Taarji, et le Président de l’Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P), Hicham El Habti. La seconde convention-cadre, relative à la mobilisation des secteurs privé et financier pour le déploiement de la feuille de route pour le développement de l’industrie nationale de défense et de sécurité, a été signée par le ministre de l’Intérieur, Abdelouafi Laftit, le ministre de l’Economie, des Finances et de la Performance publique, Fouzi Lekjaa, le ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce, de l’Investissement et de l’Inclusion économique, Ryad Mezzour, le ministre délégué auprès de la Cheffe du gouvernement, chargé de l’Administration de la Défense Nationale, Abdeltif Loudyi, le Wali de Bank Al-Maghrib, Abdellatif Jouahri, le Directeur général de l’AMDIE, Ali Seddiki, le Président du Groupement Professionnel des Banques du Maroc (GPBM), Othmane Benjelloun, le Président de la Confédération Générale des Entreprises du Maroc (CGEM), Mehdi Tazi, le Président de l’Autorité Marocaine du Marché des Capitaux (AMMC), Tarik Senhaji, le Directeur général de la Bourse de Casablanca,Nasser Seddiki, et le Président de l'Association Marocaine des Investisseurs en Capital (AMIC), Omar Bekkali. Cette cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de la Cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, du Conseiller du Roi, Fouad Ali El Himma, du Général de Corps d'Armée, Mohammed Berrid, Inspecteur Général des Forces Armées Royales, Commandant la Zone Sud et du Chambellan du Roi, Sidi Mohammed El Alaoui. The post Industrie de défense et de sécurité : le Roi préside la cérémonie de signature de deux conventions-cadres appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Southern Nigeria deserves eight years in presidency like North — Shehu Sani
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo Former Kaduna Central Senator, Shehu Sani, has said Southern Nigeria deserves to retain the Presidency for eight years, just as the North did under the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the interest of fairness, equity and justice. Sani said individual political ambitions should not be allowed to undermine the historical relationship, solidarity and common interests shared by the North and South. He spoke on Wednesday while delivering the second-term inauguration lecture of Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, in Osogbo. The former lawmaker said the principle of power rotation should be respected to ensure fairness between the two regions. “Like every other part of the country, the South deserves respect for the principle of political power rotation. Power has been held in the North for eight years. It should be allowed, in the spirit of fairness, equity and justice, to be in the South for eight years. “I am not saying this because I am in Osun State or because His Excellency is my friend or brother. Everyone who knows my history and has followed my public statements wherever I have spoken knows that this has always been my position. “The political ambitions of individuals should not be allowed to disrupt the good relationship, historical connections, commonality and solidarity that exist between the North and the South. We must not throw these values into the gutter because of the ambitions of individuals,” he said. Speaking on the theme, “Beyond the Ballot Box: Subnational Governance, Institutional Independence and the Future of Democracy in Nigeria,” Sani urged Adeleke to make his second term a period of institutional reforms, economic transformation and measurable development. He described the governor’s renewed mandate as a social contract that comes with greater expectations and responsibilities. He urged Adeleke to consolidate the achievements of his first term, address identified shortcomings and build strong institutions capable of surviving successive administrations. According to him, elections determine who occupies public offices, but strong institutions and effective governance determine whether political power translates into meaningful development. Sani also said President Bola Tinubu and Adeleke shared similar political DNA, although he did not elaborate on the comparison. In his remarks, Adeleke described Sani as a practical politician and intellectual with a deep understanding of Nigerian federalism. The governor acknowledged the challenges confronting the country’s federal structure, including excessive concentration of powers at the centre. He, however, expressed optimism that the Tinubu administration was taking steps towards restructuring the federation through constitutional amendments and the devolution of powers to states. “There is no doubt that Nigeria faces many challenges in its practice of federalism. Several commentators have alluded to the severe weaknesses of federalism as practised in Nigeria. “Repeated emphasis has been focused on heavy central government and over-centralisation of powers, among others. “But the good thing is that the Tinubu administration is already moving to restructure the federal structure. A number of legislative steps have been taken to amend the constitution. State police are coming on stream. The Exclusive Legislative List is being reduced, with more responsibilities being pushed to the states,” Adeleke said. Earlier, the Secretary to the State Government, Teslim Igbalaye, said the lecture was organised to promote discussions on preserving democracy in Nigeria. He said the choice of Sani as guest speaker was informed by his understanding of democratic principles and the country’s political challenges. The post Southern Nigeria deserves eight years in presidency like North — Shehu Sani appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police arrest three suspects over political violence in Kebbi
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested three suspects over alleged political violence during a political gathering in Zauro, Makera and surrounding communities in Birnin Kebbi Local Government Area. The arrests followed reports of violence and the alleged presence of individuals wielding dangerous weapons during political activities organised by members of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, saying preliminary investigations revealed that the gathering, reportedly presented as a distribution of relief materials, was organised by the wife of the ADC governorship candidate. According to him, the activities took place in Zauro, Makera, Gwadangwaji, Gawasu, Morida and Karyo without prior notification to the Police at least 48 hours before their commencement. Usman said the failure to notify the Police violated an agreement reached between the Command and political parties during a stakeholders’ engagement on September 7, 2026, as well as a subsequent meeting with the party’s caucus on November 2, 2026. He explained that during the meetings, the party had undertaken to notify the Commissioner of Police of all political activities at least 48 hours ahead to enable adequate security arrangements. The police spokesperson said video evidence obtained by the Command showed individuals in the convoy carrying sticks, machetes and swords, while some speakers allegedly made inciting statements capable of disrupting public peace. He added that some vehicles in the convoy were observed without registration numbers or with questionable number plates, while sirens were also used in violation of applicable traffic regulations. Usman said the Command condemned the conduct, warning that political activities must not degenerate into thuggery, violence or inflammatory statements. He said the Police would not tolerate any action capable of undermining public peace or setting a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Command urged the party’s leadership to honour its commitment to peaceful political engagement and cooperate with security agencies, including handing over individuals involved in unlawful conduct. Usman said the three suspects had been charged to court for prosecution, adding that any breach of agreed security protocols or applicable laws would be dealt with accordingly. The Command also called on relevant authorities to investigate reports of minors’ involvement in political activities and take appropriate measures to protect them from exploitation, violence and other harmful circumstances. In a related development, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Jega reported another political activity organised by the same party without prior notification to the Police. The organisers were subsequently directed to reschedule the rally and formally notify the Police to enable adequate security arrangements. The Command advised parents and guardians to caution their children and wards against being recruited or used for political violence. It warned that individuals and political parties found engaging in political violence, sponsoring thuggery or violating the law would be held accountable. The post Police arrest three suspects over political violence in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nadowli-Kaleo NPP chairman denies stealing Nkoko Nkitinkiti birds, challenges Agric Minister’s account
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) Constituency Chairman for Nadowli-Kaleo, Joseph Kontomah, has denied being arrested for stealing birds under the government’s Nkoko Nkitinkiti programme, describing the allegation as false and made by the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Eric Opoku. Mr Kontomah says he was invited to the Nadowli District Police Command for discussions after he and some constituents collected birds from a distribution centre to protest what he described as the partisan allocation of the poultry to members of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC). Addressing a press conference attended by regional and constituency party executives, as well as journalists, he said he later led his team back to the farm to return the birds following advice from the police. “I wish to state, unequivocally and without any ambiguity, that the publication is completely false, misleading and has no factual basis whatsoever,” he said. The controversy followed comments by Mr Opoku in Parliament on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, that the Nadowli-Kaleo NPP chairman had been arrested for stealing birds under the programme. “We received reports that the NPP constituency Chairman for Nadowli-Kaleo was arrested for stealing Nkoko Nkitinkiti birds. The Police have confirmed the story and have retrieved some of the birds,” the minister told the House. Mr Opoku said his ministry contacted the Nadowli-Kaleo District Police Command to verify the report before making it public. He also accused the NPP of criticising the programme in Parliament while some of its members were allegedly involved in stealing the birds. But Mr Kontomah has challenged that account, insisting that he was invited to the police station for a discussion and was not arrested. According to the NPP chairman, he received information on November 23 that the Agric Officer overseeing the programme was distributing the birds exclusively to NDC members and executives, including branch executives, coordinators and constituency officers. He said he subsequently accompanied some concerned constituents and a media team from Vision TV to the distribution centre to establish what was happening. Mr Kontomah claimed their observations confirmed the information they had received, prompting members of his team to enter the poultry house and collect some birds while the media team was present. He said the action was intended to draw attention to what he considered an unfair distribution of a publicly funded intervention, rather than to steal or unlawfully appropriate government property. “It is important to establish that this action was not an attempt to steal or unlawfully appropriate public property, as maliciously alleged. Rather, it was an expression of concern over what appeared to be a partisan distribution of a national intervention,” he said. He also said he granted a four-minute interview to Vision TV at the site, during which he appealed to the District Chief Executive, Mary Haruna, to ensure that the birds were distributed fairly among eligible constituents, irrespective of political affiliation. Mr Kontomah argued that the programme was financed with taxpayers’ money and should not be treated as an initiative for members of any political party. On the alleged arrest, Mr Kontomah said he received a telephone call from the Nadowli District Police Commander after leaving the farm, inviting him to the command for a discussion. He said he honoured the invitation and explained his concerns about the distribution process, particularly the alleged exclusion of constituents who did not belong to the NDC. According to him, the District Chief Executive was contacted during the engagement and indicated her willingness to ensure a fair distribution. He said the police commander subsequently advised him to mobilise his team to return the birds to the farm to allow for a more structured allocation process. “In compliance with this directive, by 3:00 p.m. on the same day, 23rd November 2026, I led my team, again accompanied by the media to return the birds to the farm,” he said. Mr Kontomah said the sequence of events contradicted the minister’s description of him as a thief and maintained that footage of the incident and his interview with Vision TV were available. He accused Mr Opoku of deliberately confusing a police invitation with an arrest or engaging in political propaganda. The NPP chairman said his intervention was informed partly by what he described as an earlier incident in December 2024, when more than 100 bags of fertiliser intended for farmers in the constituency were allegedly taken over and distributed among NDC supporters and party executives. He claimed similar incidents were occurring in other parts of the country and accused the governing party of prioritising its members in the distribution of public programmes. “We decided to fight this nationwide selective service of the NDC by starting from the Nadowli soil,” he said. The Nkoko Nkitinkiti initiative, formally known as the Poultry Farm-to-Table project, is part of the government’s Feed Ghana strategy. It is intended to support households, including vulnerable groups, through poultry production. The programme targets about 60,000 households across the country’s 276 constituencies, with plans to distribute three million birds. The 2027 Budget allocated GH¢245 million to the initiative as part of a broader GH¢2.9 billion allocation to the Ministry of Food and Agriculture. Mr Kontomah also criticised the Speaker of Parliament for allowing the minister to make the allegations on the floor of the House. He said the Speaker should have required Mr Opoku to provide evidence to support the claims and called for the statements to be expunged from the parliamentary record. He maintained that the allegations were intended to damage his reputation and undermine the NPP’s leadership in the constituency.

items.title: At least 3 killed, 14 injured after under-construction building collapses near Karachi's Baloch Colony
items.description: KARACHI: At least three people were killed and 14 injured on Wednesday when an under-construction building collapsed in Karachi Administration Housing Society near Baloch Colony, according to police and rescue services officials. Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that a ground-plus-five-storey building with one penthouse was constructed on 600 square yards and it collapsed when over 20 workers were present at the site. He added that rescue teams responded immediately, launching an operation with modern equipment and machinery. He said three bodies and 14 injured persons were recovered from the debris using around one dozen rescue vehicles. Meanwhile, police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed confirmed three bodies were brought to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC), adding that another 14 injured were brought to the hospital. During the initial probe, it emerged that the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) had approved only a ground-plus-one-storey building, East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi told Dawn. He held that the owner violated the approved plans, adding that when the SBCA ordered construction to halt, the owner approached the court and obtained a stay order against the authority. Subsequently, the SBCA did not take any further action. He said the building was at the final stage of construction and it had not been ascertained what caused it to collapse. Meanwhile, East senior superintendent of police (SSP) Zubair Nazir Shaikh told Dawn that three suspects, including a contractor and a family member of the building’s owner, were arrested. He also said the exact cause of the building collapse would be ascertained after proper investigation by the SBCA officials. Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi told Dawn that the “government will take strict action against those who are responsible”. Separately, the commissioner’s spokesperson, Sattar Javed, said in a statement that 12 under-construction buildings in different blocks of the Karachi Admin society had been sealed. Earlier, Sindh Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho had directed police officials to reach the incident site immediately and assist in rescue operations, according to a statement from the police spokesperson. He directed officials to ensure close coordination with Rescue 1122, the fire brigade and other relevant agencies, and take necessary measures to secure the site, remove obstacles to rescue efforts and maintain traffic flow. Rescue personnel and volunteers search for victims in the rubble of a collapsed under-construction building in Karachi on November 25, 2026. — AFP The IG also ordered that all available resources be used to rescue people potentially trapped under the rubble and that assistance be provided to ensure the injured receive immediate medical attention. He directed the traffic police to clear roads, maintain an uninterrupted flow of traffic and make arrangements for alternative routes. Relevant police officials were also instructed to personally supervise rescue operations and provide regular updates on the situation, the statement said. Rescue personnel and volunteers search for victims in the rubble of a collapsed under-construction building in Karachi on November 25, 2026. — AFP SBCA planned to demolish building: Mayor Wahab Speaking to the media at the site, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab confirmed that the SBCA had planned to demolish the building. However, the authority had been unable to do so due to a stay order, he said. “If there had been no stay order, this building would have been demolished,” he said, underscoring the need to “exercise responsibility”. “The portion mafia and corrupt elements have caused many losses to this city,” he said. Wahab also noted that there was “political influence” behind the construction. However, he regretted that when the administration tried to take action, a stay order came from the courts. The Karachi mayor said that he would discuss the matter with the Sindh chief minister and the local government minister. “Strict action must be taken to prevent this in future,” he said. Sindh CM directs SBCA to examine possible negligence, vows strict action Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to reach the site and expedite rescue operations, said a statement from the Chief Minister House. He also visited the site to review the ongoing rescue operation, where he was briefed by Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, DC East Nasrullah Abbasi and Rescue 1122 personnel on the progress of rescue efforts and the arrangements for providing medical treatment to the injured. Speaking to the media, CM Murad said the exact number of people inside the building at the time of the collapse remained unclear due to multiple contractors working at the site. According to information received from the affected families, around 10 people were reported missing, although rescue officials were still verifying the final number, he added. Rescue personnel and volunteers search for victims in the rubble of a collapsed under-construction building in Karachi on November 25, 2026. — AFP According to the chief minister, the building had reportedly been approved for only two floors, including the ground floor, but six floors had been constructed. Expressing serious concern over the illegal construction, he questioned the role of the SBCA and other relevant departments, stressing that such large-scale violations could not have taken place without the possible involvement or negligence of government officials. CM Murad said the building owner, consultant, contractor and any government officials found involved would be held accountable for the incident, which he termed not merely an accident but a case of criminal negligence. He vowed that those responsible for the loss of lives would face strict punishment and that justice would be ensured for the affected families. He warned that negligence by the SBCA or district administration would not be tolerated, adding that officials found responsible would face strict legal action, including imprisonment. The chief minister also directed authorities to immediately inspect nearby buildings to ensure public safety. He was briefed on the medical facilities being provided to the injured, instructing hospital administrations to remain on high alert and ensure that no negligence occurred in their treatment. He reaffirmed that the rescue operation remained a priority and that all possible measures would be taken to recover missing persons and bring those responsible for the tragedy to justice. CM Murad directed the relevant authorities to utilise all available resources to rescue anyone potentially trapped beneath the rubble. He also urged media personnel and citizens to maintain a safe distance so that rescue teams could carry out their operations without obstruction. In his earlier statement, CM Murad had directed Rescue 1122, the district administration, police and other relevant agencies to coordinate and complete the rescue operation. He directed the SBCA to examine the building’s approved plans, construction standards and any possible negligence. The administration was also ordered to determine the cause of the collapse and identify those responsible in case of negligence or illegal construction. The chief minister also directed the Karachi commissioner and relevant agencies to continuously monitor the rescue operation and submit a detailed report on the building collapse. President, PM express condolences President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow at the incident and called for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the building collapse, according to a statement issued by his office. He added that the investigation should examine construction standards, building plans, and oversight provided by relevant authorities. He directed the Sindh government to take action against those responsible. President Zardari directed all available resources to be utilised to recover individuals trapped under the rubble and accelerate the rescue operation. He also directed the best possible medical care for the injured. He further instructed that a safety assessment should be carried out on the surrounding buildings. “There is no room for any lapse in the discharge of duties by relevant institutions regarding the construction and safety of buildings,” the statement said. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also expressed sorrow at the building collapse and offered condolences to the bereaved family, Radio Pakistan reported. He directed the authorities to ensure priority medical treatment for the injured, the report added. Roof and building collapses are common across Pakistan, mainly because of poor safety standards and the use of shoddy construction materials. But Karachi, home to more than 20 million, is especially notorious for poor construction, illegal extensions, ageing infrastructure, overcrowding and lax enforcement of building regulations. In September, five people were killed and two others injured when a wall of the dilapidated building of a government school collapsed on them in Orangi Town. Earlier this year, at least 15 people, including women and children, were killed, and 18 others were injured after a gas explosion caused part of a residential building to collapse in Karachi’s Soldier Bazaar area. In July 2025, at least 27 people died, and 10 others were injured after a five-storey building collapsed in the Lyari area of the metropolis. The building had already been declared uninhabitable by authorities due to its dilapidated structure.

items.title: FIFM : Goldblum, sous le charme de Marrakech, se verrait bien en méchant de James Bond
items.description: Après avoir reçu l’Étoile d’or du Festival international du film de Marrakech, Jeff Goldblum s’est prêté au jeu de la table ronde. Entre souvenirs de carrière, réflexion sur le métier d’acteur, vieillissement, personnages complexes et projets rêvés, l’acteur américain s’est surtout laissé aller à quelques confidences. Parmi elles, une envie assumée : incarner un méchant dans le prochain James Bond. À Marrakech, Goldblum a également évoqué avec enthousiasme les lieux mythiques de la ville et les figures qui y ont laissé leur empreinte. Interrogé sur le rôle ou le genre de film qu’il rêverait encore d’explorer après une carrière aussi riche, Jeff Goldblum n’a pas longtemps hésité. « Je meurs d’envie de travailler avec des réalisateurs avec lesquels je n’ai pas encore tourné », explique-t-il d’abord. Mais l’un des projets qu’il cite spontanément est particulièrement savoureux : James Bond. L’acteur ne se voit pas forcément dans le costume de l’agent 007. « Ils ne vont pas me choisir pour jouer James Bond », lance-t-il avec humour. Mais il se verrait parfaitement de l’autre côté du miroir : « Peut-être que je pourrais jouer un méchant dans un James Bond ! Ce serait génial. » Goldblum assume son enthousiasme pour la franchise, tout comme pour ceux qui portent actuellement le prochain chapitre de la saga. Il cite notamment Robert Pattinson et Denis Villeneuve, dont il apprécie le travail. Une déclaration qui lui ressemble : après avoir incarné des personnages aussi différents que le scientifique Seth Brundle dans « La Mouche », le docteur Ian Malcolm dans « Jurassic Park », Zeus dans « Kaos » ou encore le magicien d’« Wicked », l’acteur semble davantage attiré par la complexité d’un personnage que par son statut. « Je les inviterais tous ! » À Marrakech, Goldblum s’est également prêté à un exercice particulièrement cinéphile. Interrogé sur la personnalité avec laquelle il aimerait passer une soirée à La Mamounia parmi Winston Churchill, Charlie Chaplin, Alfred Hitchcock et Paul McCartney, il refuse finalement de choisir. « Je les inviterais tous ! », répond-il. Le choix n’était pourtant pas simple. Churchill l’intéresse pour son rôle historique, Chaplin pour son parcours artistique, Hitchcock pour son cinéma et ses entretiens, tandis que Paul McCartney occupe une place particulière dans son univers musical. L’acteur raconte d’ailleurs avoir rencontré l’ancien Beatles l’année précédente, dans les coulisses d’un spectacle de George Clooney. Une rencontre qu’il décrit comme particulièrement chaleureuse. Mais le lieu de la question semble également l’avoir intrigué. Lorsqu’on lui rappelle que Paul McCartney a consacré une chanson à La Mamounia, Goldblum découvre l’anecdote avec surprise et se met même à fredonner quelques notes de « Mamunia ». La séquence révèle aussi quelque chose du rapport de Goldblum à Marrakech. L’acteur ne semble pas considérer sa venue au festival comme une simple étape promotionnelle. Depuis la cérémonie d’hommage qui lui a été consacrée, il multiplie les références à la ville, au Maroc et à l’accueil qui lui a été réservé. Sa présence au FIFM intervient ainsi dans un environnement chargé d’histoire cinématographique et culturelle, un contexte qui semble particulièrement correspondre à sa curiosité. Cette curiosité est d’ailleurs au cœur de sa manière de concevoir son métier. Goldblum explique préférer le travail collectif à l’idée de créer seul, insistant sur l’importance de la rencontre avec les réalisateurs et les autres acteurs. « J'adore être dirigé, surtout par de bons réalisateurs » , affirme-t-il, tout en défendant la nécessité de conserver sa propre identité artistique. « Les bons rôles sont multidimensionnels » Lors de la table ronde, l’acteur est également revenu sur ces personnages à la fois puissants et fragiles qui ont marqué sa filmographie. Il dit être attiré par les personnages « complexes », « multidimensionnels », capables de réunir plusieurs facettes contradictoires. Pour Goldblum, cette complexité n’est finalement qu’un reflet de la nature humaine. Un individu peut être puissant et fragile, intelligent et stupide, empathique et brutal, parfois au même moment. « Les bons rôles, si le scénario est bien écrit, offrent la possibilité de faire un peu de tout ça » , estime-t-il. Cette approche éclaire une carrière construite justement sur des personnages difficiles à enfermer dans une seule catégorie. De « La Mouche » à « Jurassic Park », de Wes Anderson à « Wicked », Goldblum a constamment cultivé cette part d’étrangeté et de contradiction. Vieillir, réussir : « trouver sa propre définition » À Marrakech, Goldblum a aussi livré une réflexion plus personnelle sur le vieillissement, la masculinité et le succès. Face au vieillissement, il défend « l’acceptation » et la capacité à composer avec ce qui change, plutôt que de chercher à le dissimuler. Sur la masculinité, il appelle à se débarrasser des « vieilles idées dépassées et poussiéreuses ». Quant au succès, il refuse de le réduire à l’argent, au statut ou à l’accumulation. Pour lui, il s’agit avant tout de se connaître, de créer du lien et d’avoir un impact positif sur les autres. À 70 ans passés, Jeff Goldblum ne donne surtout pas l’impression de vouloir ralentir. Son discours est celui d’un acteur qui continue à chercher, à apprendre et à se laisser surprendre. Son envie d’un rôle de méchant dans James Bond résume finalement assez bien cette disposition : ne pas regarder sa carrière comme un parcours achevé, mais comme une succession de possibilités encore ouvertes. Et à Marrakech, entre les souvenirs de cinéma, les rencontres et les projets rêvés, Jeff Goldblum continue visiblement à cultiver ce qui semble être l’un de ses moteurs essentiels : la curiosité. The post FIFM : Goldblum, sous le charme de Marrakech, se verrait bien en méchant de James Bond appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Assemblée nationale/5ᵉ séance plénière de la 2ᵉ session ordinaire : Quatre lois définitivement adoptées et une en première lecture
items.description: Lomé, 25 nov. (ATOP) – Les députés ont définitivement adopté quatre lois puis examiné, en première lecture le projet de loi portant création, missions, organisation et fonctionnement de la Caisse des dépôts et consignations (CDC) en République togolaise. Ces textes ont été examinés lors de la 5ᵉ séance plénière de la 2ᵉ session ordinaire, tenue le mardi 24 novembre au siège de l’institution. Les quatre lois adoptées définitivement portent sur l’orientation agricole, la protection physique des matières nucléaires, la responsabilité civile en matière de dommages nucléaires et la réparation complémentaire des dommages nucléaires. La loi adoptée en première lecture vise à créer une CDC, qui agira en qualité de tiers de confiance chargé de centraliser et de gérer des ressources. La CDC aura pour mission de collecter, recevoir et conserver les fonds publics et privés mis à sa disposition, ainsi que les dépôts et consignations administratifs et judiciaires et les cautionnements. Elle sera également chargée de gérer les fonds reçus au moyen de placements sécurisés et rentables, et de contribuer au financement des projets de développement. L’adoption de cette loi permettra de renforcer l’architecture du système financier national et de répondre durablement aux insuffisances constatées dans le financement de secteurs prioritaires, notamment le logement social, la santé, l’éducation et les énergies renouvelables. Le président de l’Assemblée nationale a présenté la CDC comme un établissement public à caractère spécial, doté de la personnalité morale et de l’autonomie de gestion administrative et financière, placé sous la tutelle du ministre chargé des Finances et investi d’une mission d’intérêt général. Il a souligné que la caisse contribuera au financement endogène à long terme en centralisant et en gérant des ressources aujourd’hui souvent peu rentables, dormantes ou insuffisamment sécurisées. Il a également estimé que l’épargne nationale doit servir le développement du pays et que la rigueur financière peut aller de pair avec l’ambition et la confiance. Le ministre des Finances et du Budget, Barcola Essowè Georges, a indiqué que la CDC facilitera la modernisation du système financier national et le rapprochement du cadre institutionnel des meilleures pratiques internationales. Selon lui, elle favorisera une mobilisation accrue des ressources nationales et ouvrira de nouvelles possibilités de financement pour des projets structurants à fort impact socio-économique. Le ministre a ajouté que la Caisse de dépôt permettra de mieux maîtriser le recours à l’endettement extérieur, de renforcer la résilience financière de l’État et de soutenir la transformation structurelle de l’économie. ATOP/AR/JK/BV
